Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatada, who said: "When the verse was revealed: ﴿The reckoning of people has drawn near to them﴾ (21:1), some people said: 'The Hour has indeed drawn near,' so they desisted. The people desisted a little, then returned to their deeds, the deeds of evil. So Allah revealed: ﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it﴾ (16:1). Then some people of misguidance said: 'This is the command of Allah, it has come.' So the people desisted, then returned to their plotting, the evil plotting. So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿And if We delay the punishment from them until a counted community﴾."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and al-Hakim (who graded it sound) related from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿until a counted community﴾, he said: "until a counted term."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related from Qatada regarding ﴿They will surely say, "What is holding it back?"﴾: "meaning the people of hypocrisy."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Suddi regarding His saying: ﴿And what they used to mock at encompassed them﴾: he said, "meaning the punishment they mocked befell them."

The lam in ﴿وَلَئِنْ أَذَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ﴾ is the lam introducing an oath (al-lam al-muwatti'a lil-qasam). Al-insan is the genus, so it includes both the believer and the disbeliever. The exception in ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا﴾ indicates this. It has also been said that the intended meaning is the genus of disbelievers. This is supported by the fact that despair, ingratitude, exultation and boasting are, for the most part, the attributes of the people of disbelief, not of the people of Islam. It has also been said that the intended person is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, and it has been said that he is Abdullah ibn Umayya al-Makhzumi.

By mercy here is meant blessing: abundant provision, health, and safety from trials. ﴿ثُمَّ نَزَعْنَاهَا مِنْهُ﴾ means that We take it away from him. ﴿إِنَّهُ لَيَئُوسٌ﴾ means he is despairing of mercy, greatly hopeless of its return and of the like of it. ﴿كَفُورٌ﴾ means one who is greatly ungrateful, and it is denial of it (al-juhud biha), as Ibn al-A'rabi said. The use of the two intensive forms (sigha al-mubalagha) in ﴿لَيَئُوسٌ كَفُورٌ﴾ indicates that man is greatly prone to despair and greatly prone to denial when God takes away some of his blessings. So he does not hope for their return, and he does not give thanks for what he previously had of them.

The use of the word "taste" (al-dhawq) indicates that this behaviour occurs in him when even the least blessing that God bestows upon him is taken away, because tasting (al-idhaqa wa-l-dhawq) is the least by which taste is perceived.

Al-na'ma' is a favour whose effect appears upon its recipient, and al-darra' is the appearance of the effect of harm upon the one afflicted by it.

The meaning is: if God, glory be to Him, makes His servant taste His favour of health, safety and wealth, after he had been in hardship, whether poverty, sickness or fear, he does not respond to that with the gratitude that befits him toward God, glory be to Him. Rather, he says: ﴿ذَهَبَ السَّيِّئَاتُ عَنِّي﴾, that is, the calamities which had troubled him, of hardship, poverty, fear and sickness, have gone away from him and their effect has ceased, while he is not thankful to God nor praising Him for His blessings. ﴿إِنَّهُ لَفَرِحٌ فَخُورٌ﴾ means greatly joyful in insolence and arrogance, greatly boastful toward people and haughty over them because of the blessings with which God has favoured him. The expression of the harm reaching him by the word "touch" (al-mass) is appropriate to the expression of favour by "tasting" (al-idhaqa), since both refer to the least thing to which the term "encounter" (al-mulaqah) can apply, as has been mentioned previously.

﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا﴾: for their custom is patience when trials descend, and gratitude when blessings are received.

Al-Akhfash said: this is an exception that is not from the first part; that is, "but those who are patient and do righteous deeds during both states of blessing and affliction."

Al-Farra' said: it is an exception from the subject of ﴿لَئِنْ أَذَقْنَاهُ﴾, that is, from al-insan, since al-insan means al-nas (people), and al-nas includes the disbeliever and the believer, so it is a continuous exception (istithna' muttasil). The reference in ﴿أُولَئِكَ﴾ is to the relative pronoun (al-mawsul) in terms of its being characterised by patience and doing righteous deeds. ﴿لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ﴾ means forgiveness for their sins, and ﴿وَأَجْرٌ كَبِيرٌ﴾ means a reward they will be rewarded with for their good deeds, great and utterly immense.

Then God, glory be to Him, consoled His Messenger ﷺ, saying: ﴿فَلَعَلَّكَ تَارِكٌ بَعْضَ مَا يُوحَى إِلَيْكَ﴾ (p-650), that is: perhaps, because of the enormity of what you see from them of disbelief and denial, and their demanding of signs according to their desires and their obstinacy, you are leaving aside some of what is revealed to you, of what God has sent down to you and commanded you to convey, of what is hard for them to hear or find difficult to act upon, such as reviling their gods and commanding them to believe in God alone.

It has been said: this statement is in the form of a question, that is, "Are you leaving it aside?" It has also been said that it has the meaning of negation with disapproval, that is: "This does not come from you; rather, you convey to them all that God has sent down to you, whether they love it or dislike it, whether they will or refuse."

﴿وَضَائِقٌ بِهِ صَدْرُكَ﴾ is conjoined to تَارِكٌ. The pronoun in بِهِ refers to مَا or to بَعْضَ. He expressed it with ضَائِقٌ rather than ضَيِّقٌ, because the active participle (ism al-fa'il) in it carries the meaning of occurrence and onset, while the adjective in the pattern of the attributive (al-sifah al-mushabbahah) carries the meaning of permanence.

﴿أَنْ يَقُولُوا﴾ means: lest they say, or fearing that they will say, or so that they will not say: ﴿لَوْلَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ كَنْزٌ﴾, that is: why was a treasure not sent down to him, that is, hidden stored wealth from which he could benefit? ﴿أَوْ جَاءَ مَعَهُ مَلَكٌ﴾ means an angel who would confirm him and show us the validity of his message.

Then God, glory be to Him, explained that the state of His Messenger ﷺ is restricted to warning, so He said: ﴿إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ نَذِيرٌ﴾: it is not incumbent upon you except to warn of what has been revealed to you, and it is not incumbent upon you to achieve their demands or to fulfil their proposals. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَكِيلٌ﴾ means He preserves what they say, and He does with them what must be done.

His saying: ﴿أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَرَاهُ﴾: أَمْ here is the disjunctive أَمْ (al-munqati'ah) which has the meaning of بَلْ together with the interrogative hamzah. It turns away from what came before of their negligence toward the revelation and their not being content with what he brought of the clear miracles, and begins to mention their committing what is worse than that, namely their accusation against him that he invented it. The interrogation is for rebuke and reproach. The hidden pronoun in افْتَرَاهُ refers to the Prophet ﷺ, and the explicit pronoun refers to what is revealed.

Then God, glory be to Him, commanded him to answer them with what will silence them, expose their lies and manifest their incapacity, so He said: ﴿قُلْ فَأْتُوا بِعَشْرِ سُوَرٍ مِثْلِهِ﴾, that is, similar to it in eloquence, excellence of arrangement, solidity of wording and grandeur of meanings. He described the surahs with what is used to describe the singular, saying مِثْلَهُنَّ and not أَمْثَالَهُ, because the intended meaning is the similarity of each one of the surahs, or for the purpose of indicating the aspect of resemblance, the basis of which is similarity in one thing, namely eloquence reaching the limit of inimitability. This is only so according to the view that agreement in the plural, dual and singular is a condition.

Then He described the surahs with another attribute, saying: ﴿مُفْتَرَيَاتٍ﴾ (invented). ﴿وَادْعُوا﴾ (and call upon) is for the purpose of seeking aid in the challenge with the ten surahs. ﴿مَنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ﴾ means whoever you are able to call upon and are capable of seeking help from of this human species, and from those you worship and make partners with God, glory be to Him.

His saying: ﴿مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ is connected to ادْعُوا: that is, call upon whomever you can, passing beyond God, the Exalted. ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ means in what you claim of my having invented it.

﴿فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا لَكُمْ﴾: that is, if they do not do what you asked of them and what you challenged them with, namely bringing ten similar surahs, and they do not respond to the required counter-challenge. The pronoun in لَكُمْ may refer to the Messenger of God ﷺ and the believers, or to the Prophet ﷺ alone, in the plural form out of glorification and majesty. ﴿فَاعْلَمُوا﴾ is a command addressed to the Messenger of God ﷺ and the believers, or to the Messenger alone according to the interpretation mentioned shortly before.

The meaning of commanding them with knowledge is commanding them to remain steadfast in it, since they already know this before the disbelievers' incapacity to bring ten similar surahs. Or the intended meaning of the command with knowledge is the command to increase in it, to a degree that no doubt mixes with it and no uncertainty pervades it, which is certainty of knowledge (ilm al-yaqin). The first is preferable.

The meaning of ﴿أَنَّمَا أُنْزِلَ بِعِلْمِ اللَّهِ﴾ is that it was sent down accompanied by the knowledge of God, which is specific to Him, whose reality minds cannot grasp and whose meaning intellects cannot clarify, because of the inimitability it contains, which lies beyond human capacity. ﴿وَأَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ﴾ means: and know that God is the one singular in divinity, with no partner, and no one other than Him can do what He can do.

Then He concluded the verse with His saying: ﴿فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾, that is: will you be steadfast in Islam, sincere toward it, increasing in acts of obedience? Because you have obtained, through the disbelievers' incapacity to produce the like of ten surahs of this Book, a tranquillity beyond what you were upon and an additional insight. And even if you were Muslims before this, steadfastness in it, increase of insight in it and tranquillity through it are demanded of you.

It has been said that the pronoun in ﴿فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا﴾ refers to the relative pronoun in ﴿مَنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ﴾, and the pronoun in لَكُمْ refers to the disbelievers whom the Messenger of God challenged, and likewise the pronoun in فَاعْلَمُوا.

The meaning is: if those whom you called upon to support and assist you in producing ten surahs, from among the rest of the disbelievers and those whom they worship, and who claim that they can harm and benefit, do not respond to you, then know that this Qur'an which God has sent down upon this Messenger is beyond the power of anyone other than Him, glory be to Him and exalted, because of the inimitability it contains, which the strength of created beings falls short of. And know that it was sent down with the knowledge of God, which no minds encompass and no understandings reach. And know that He alone is singular in divinity, with no partner. ﴿فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ بَعْدَ هَذَا مُسْلِمُونَ﴾? That is: will you, after this, enter into Islam, follow its rulings and be guided by its laws?

This interpretation is stronger than the first in one respect and weaker in another. Its strength lies in the coherence of the pronouns, their harmony, and the absence of any need for some of them to be interpreted. Its weakness lies in the fact that the ordering of the command to know upon the non-response of those they called upon and sought help from is somewhat obscure and requires strained interpretation, namely that the non-response of those whom they called upon and sought help from, from among the disbelievers and the idols, despite their eagerness for their support, their backing, their exertion for their not believing, and their persistence in disbelief, indicates that these disbelievers come to know that this Qur'an is from God, and that God, glory be to Him, is the sole God with no partner, and this necessitates their entry into Islam.

Know that the challenge to the disbelievers to counter the Qur'an has varied. At times it was made with the whole Qur'an, as in His saying: ﴿قُلْ لَئِنِ اجْتَمَعَتِ الْإِنْسُ وَالْجِنُّ عَلَى أَنْ يَأْتُوا بِمِثْلِ هَذَا الْقُرْآنِ لَا يَأْتُونَ بِمِثْلِهِ﴾ [al-Isra' 17:88], and at times with ten surahs as in this verse, because ten is the first of the units of counting, and at times with a single surah, as has been mentioned previously, because a surah is the smallest portion of it.

Then God, glory be to Him, threatened whoever has a mind restricted to this world, who seeks nothing else and desires nothing beyond it, saying: ﴿مَنْ كَانَ يُرِيدُ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا وَزِينَتَهَا نُوَفِّ إِلَيْهِمْ أَعْمَالَهُمْ فِيهَا﴾.

Al-Farra' said: كَانَ here is superfluous (za'idah), and for this reason the answer is in the jussive (juzima al-jawab).

Al-Zajjaj said: مَنْ in كَانَ is in a position of jazm as a conditional particle, and its answer is نُوَفِّ إِلَيْهِمْ, that is: whoever wills (man yakun yurid).

The people of tafsir differed regarding this verse. Al-Dahhak said: it was revealed concerning the disbelievers, and al-Nahhas preferred this on the basis of the following verse: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَيْسَ لَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ إِلَّا النَّارُ﴾. It has also been said: the verse is general in application to people, both disbelievers and Muslims.

The meaning is that whoever intends by his deed the portion of this world is rewarded accordingly. By its adornment is meant what embellishes and beautifies it: health, security, abundance of provision, elevation of status, the effectiveness of one's word, and the like.

The inclusion of كَانَ in the verse indicates that they are constantly intending the world by their deeds and hardly intend the Hereafter. For this reason it has been said that, despite being given their portion of this world, they will be punished in the Hereafter, because they have restricted their intention to this world and did not act for the Hereafter.

The apparent meaning of His saying ﴿نُوَفِّ إِلَيْهِمْ أَعْمَالَهُمْ فِيهَا﴾ is that whoever intends his deed for this world will receive the worldly recompense without doubt. But what actually occurs in reality contradicts this, for not every person who desires attains his wish from this world even if he works for it and intends it. Therefore this must be restricted by the will of God, glory be to Him.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 11, verses 13–17 (part 2 of 2):

Al-Qurtubi said: Most scholars hold that this verse is unrestricted (muṭlaq), and so is the verse in al-Shura: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of this world, We will give him of it﴾ [al-Shura: 20], and likewise ﴿Whoever desires the reward of this world, then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter﴾ [al-Nisa': 134]. The verse in Subhan, ﴿Whoever desires the hasty (life), We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We wish﴾ [al-Isra': 18], restricts and explains these verses. His saying, ﴿and therein they will not be deprived﴾, means: these who desire by their deeds the life of this world, therein, that is, in this world, they will not be deprived, that is, they will not be given less of their recompense in it according to their deeds for it. This is generally the case but is not invariable; rather, it applies if His Will, glorified is He, so decrees, and His perfect wisdom favours it.

Al-Qadi said: The meaning of the verse is: whoever, by doing good, intends the life of this world and its adornment, We will pay them their deeds in full, complete, without deficiency in this world, which is what they receive of health, sufficiency, and all other pleasures and benefits. Thus the recompense is specified with what he mentioned, and it is granted to every worker for this world, even if it is little and slight.

His saying, ﴿Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter except the Fire﴾: the reference is to the aforementioned seekers. It is necessary to restrict this to those who did not intend the Hereafter by any of the deeds that count and that merit a good recompense in the abode of the Hereafter; or the verse may be specific to the disbelievers, as was mentioned earlier. ﴿And what they did is rendered void﴾, meaning: there became manifest in the Hereafter the nullification of what they did of deeds whose form was the form of acts of obedience that merit the otherworldly recompense, had they not corrupted them through corruption of their intentions, lack of sincerity, and desiring what is with Allah in the abode of recompense, but restricting that to this world and its adornment. Then Allah, glorified is He, judged their deeds as void, saying: ﴿and vain is what they used to do﴾, that is, their deed was in itself vain and not counted, because it was not done for a valid purpose that merits recompense, and what follows from a valid deed does not follow from it.

His saying, ﴿Is one who is upon a clear proof from his Lord﴾: Allah, glorified is He, made clear that there is a vast difference and a great disparity between one who seeks only this world and one who seeks the Hereafter. The meaning is: Is one who is upon a clear proof from his Lord, in following the Prophet (ﷺ) and in faith in Allah, like others who desire the life of this world and its adornment? It has also been said that what is meant by "one who is upon a clear proof from his Lord" is the Prophet (ﷺ), that is: Is one who has with him a clear evidence from Allah and a miracle, like the Qur'an, and has with him a witness like Jibril, and whom the earlier scriptures foretold, like one who desires the life of this world and its adornment?

The meaning of bayyinah (clear proof) is the argument that indicates the truth. The pronoun in His saying ﴿and a witness recites it﴾ refers to the bayyinah, considering its interpretation as argument. The pronoun in ﴿from Him﴾ refers either to the Qur'an, since it was mentioned earlier in His saying ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"﴾, or it refers to Allah, exalted is He.

The meaning is: and there follows the proof, which is the bayyinah, a witness who testifies to its truth from the Qur'an, or from Allah, glorified is He.

The witness (shahid) is the inimitability (i'jaz) that exists in the Qur'an, or the miracles that appeared to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for these are among the witnesses that accompany the Qur'an.

Al-Farra' said: Some have said: ﴿and a witness recites it, from Him﴾ is the Gospel. Even though it came before, it recites the Qur'an in confirmation. The pronoun in ﴿from Him﴾ refers to Allah, mighty and majestic is He. It has also been said that what is meant by ﴿one who is upon a clear proof from his Lord﴾ is the believers among the People of the Book, such as Abd Allah ibn Salam and his like.

His saying, ﴿and before it was the Book of Musa﴾, is conjoined to "witness," and the implied sense is: and there recites the witness another witness, from before it, which is the Book of Musa. Though it preceded in revelation, it recites the witness in testimony. He placed the witness before the Book of Musa, though the latter is earlier in existence, because the witness is a constant, inseparable attribute, so it is more firmly an attribute than the Book of Musa.

The meaning of the testimony of the Book of Musa, which is the Torah, is that it gave good tidings of Muhammad (ﷺ) and informed that he is a Messenger from Allah.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: and there recites it, from before it, the Book of Musa, because the Prophet (ﷺ) is described in the Book of Musa; they find him written with them in the Torah and the Gospel.

Abu Hatim related from some of them that he recited ﴿and before it the Book of Musa﴾ with a fatha (naṣb), and al-Mahdawi related it from al-Kalbi. Then it is conjoined to the pronoun in "yatluhu" (recites it). The meaning is: Jibril recites the Book of Musa. The accusative of ﴿imaman wa-rahmah﴾ (as a leader and a mercy) is in the sense of a circumstantial state (ḥāl).

Imam: the one who is followed and taken as a model in religion. Rahmah (mercy): the great blessing which Allah bestowed upon those to whom it was sent and upon those after them, in respect of the legal rulings it contains which agree with the ruling of the Qur'an.

The indication in His saying ﴿those﴾ refers to those characterized by that virtuous attribute, which is being upon a clear proof from Allah. The demonstrative is the subject and its predicate is ﴿believe in it﴾, that is, they affirm the Prophet (ﷺ) or the Qur'an. ﴿And whoever disbelieves in it among the factions﴾, that is, in the Prophet or in the Qur'an.

The factions (al-ahzab) are those who banded together against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), from the people of Makkah and others, or those who banded together from among the adherents of all religions. ﴿Then the Fire is his promised place﴾: that is, he is certainly among the people of the Fire. In making the Fire a "promised place" there is an indication that in it are kinds of torment that description cannot encompass. Similar is the saying of Hassan:

You brought them to the watering-places of death, while burning, so the Fire is their promised place, and death is meeting them.

﴿So do not be in doubt about it﴾, that is, do not be in doubt about the Qur'an. In this there is an implicit address to others than the Prophet (ﷺ), since he is protected from doubt about the Qur'an, (p-652) or the phrase refers to the promised place. ﴿Indeed it is the truth from your Lord﴾, so there is no room for doubt about it in any state whatsoever. ﴿But most of the people do not believe﴾ in that, despite the obligation of belief in it and the manifestation of the proofs that necessitate it. They are obstinate while knowing it is the truth, or their hearts have been sealed, so they do not understand that it is the truth at all.

Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿Then are you Muslims?﴾, that he said: it is addressed to the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Anas, regarding His saying ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment﴾, that he said: it was revealed concerning the Jews and the Christians.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abd Allah ibn Ma'bad, who said: A man stood up before Ali and said: "Inform us about this verse: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world﴾ up to His saying ﴿and vain is what they used to do.﴾" He said: "Woe to you! That refers to one who desires only this world and does not desire the Hereafter."

Al-Nahhas narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world﴾, that is, its reward and its adornment, its wealth: ﴿We will pay them﴾, that is, We will give them in full, with health, joy in family, wealth, and children; ﴿and therein they will not be deprived﴾, not be diminished. Then it was abrogated (naskh), by His saying ﴿Whoever desires the hasty (life), We hasten for him therein what We will﴾ [al-Isra': 18], the verse.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated the like of this from al-Suddi.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse that he said: whoever does a righteous deed seeking worldly gain, whether fasting, prayer, or night vigil, and does it only to seek the world, Allah says: "We will pay the one who sought in the world what he did, and his deed is nullified, and he, in the Hereafter, is among the losers."

Ibn Jarir narrated from al-Dahhak, who said: This verse was revealed concerning the people of polytheism.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿We will pay them their deeds﴾, that he said: their good things.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated the like of this from Ibn Jurayj.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿and what they did therein is rendered void﴾, that he said: what they did of good was nullified and became void in the Hereafter; for them there is no recompense therein.

Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid regarding the verse, that he said: they are the people of riya' (showing off).

Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu'aym in al-Ma'rifah narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: There is not a man of Quraysh but that a portion of the Qur'an was revealed concerning him. A man said to him: "What was revealed concerning you?" He said: "Have you not read the surah of Hud: ﴿Is one who is upon a clear proof from his Lord and a witness recites it from Him﴾? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the clear proof from his Lord, and I am the witness from Him."

Ibn Asakir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from another route from him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿Is one who is upon a clear proof from his Lord﴾: I; ﴿and a witness recites it from Him﴾: Ali."

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Abu al-Aliyah regarding His saying ﴿Is one who is upon a clear proof from his Lord﴾, that he said: that is Muhammad (ﷺ).

Abu al-Shaykh narrated the like of this from Ibrahim.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: I said to my father: "People claim, regarding Allah's saying ﴿and a witness recites it from Him﴾, that you are the reciter." He said: "I wish I were he, but it is the tongue of Muhammad (ﷺ)."

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that the witness is Jibril. Sa'id ibn Jubayr agreed with him.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through several routes from Ibn Abbas, who said: Jibril is the witness from Allah concerning what he recites of the Book of Allah which was revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And before it the Book of Musa﴾: he said: before it was the Torah upon the tongue of Musa, just as he recited the Qur'an upon the tongue of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Asakir narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali, regarding His saying ﴿and a witness recites it from Him﴾, that he said: Muhammad is the witness from Allah.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿and before it the Book of Musa﴾, that he said: before it the Book came to Musa.

Abd al-Razzaq and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah regarding ﴿and whoever disbelieves in it among the factions﴾, that he said: the disbelievers are factions, all of them upon disbelief.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah, who said: regarding ﴿and whoever disbelieves in it among the factions﴾: from among the Jews and the Christians.

The lam in ﴿وَلَئِنْ أَذَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ﴾ is the lam introducing an oath (al-lam al-muwatti'a lil-qasam). Al-insan is the genus, so it includes both the believer and the disbeliever. The exception in ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا﴾ indicates this. It has also been said that the intended meaning is the genus of disbelievers. This is supported by the fact that despair, ingratitude, exultation and boasting are, for the most part, the attributes of the people of disbelief, not of the people of Islam. It has also been said that the intended person is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, and it has been said that he is Abdullah ibn Umayya al-Makhzumi.

By mercy here is meant blessing: abundant provision, health, and safety from trials. ﴿ثُمَّ نَزَعْنَاهَا مِنْهُ﴾ means that We take it away from him. ﴿إِنَّهُ لَيَئُوسٌ﴾ means he is despairing of mercy, greatly hopeless of its return and of the like of it. ﴿كَفُورٌ﴾ means one who is greatly ungrateful, and it is denial of it (al-juhud biha), as Ibn al-A'rabi said. The use of the two intensive forms (sigha al-mubalagha) in ﴿لَيَئُوسٌ كَفُورٌ﴾ indicates that man is greatly prone to despair and greatly prone to denial when God takes away some of his blessings. So he does not hope for their return, and he does not give thanks for what he previously had of them.

The use of the word "taste" (al-dhawq) indicates that this behaviour occurs in him when even the least blessing that God bestows upon him is taken away, because tasting (al-idhaqa wa-l-dhawq) is the least by which taste is perceived.

Al-na'ma' is a favour whose effect appears upon its recipient, and al-darra' is the appearance of the effect of harm upon the one afflicted by it.

The meaning is: if God, glory be to Him, makes His servant taste His favour of health, safety and wealth, after he had been in hardship, whether poverty, sickness or fear, he does not respond to that with the gratitude that befits him toward God, glory be to Him. Rather, he says: ﴿ذَهَبَ السَّيِّئَاتُ عَنِّي﴾, that is, the calamities which had troubled him, of hardship, poverty, fear and sickness, have gone away from him and their effect has ceased, while he is not thankful to God nor praising Him for His blessings. ﴿إِنَّهُ لَفَرِحٌ فَخُورٌ﴾ means greatly joyful in insolence and arrogance, greatly boastful toward people and haughty over them because of the blessings with which God has favoured him. The expression of the harm reaching him by the word "touch" (al-mass) is appropriate to the expression of favour by "tasting" (al-idhaqa), since both refer to the least thing to which the term "encounter" (al-mulaqah) can apply, as has been mentioned previously.

﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا﴾: for their custom is patience when trials descend, and gratitude when blessings are received.

Al-Akhfash said: this is an exception that is not from the first part; that is, "but those who are patient and do righteous deeds during both states of blessing and affliction."

Al-Farra' said: it is an exception from the subject of ﴿لَئِنْ أَذَقْنَاهُ﴾, that is, from al-insan, since al-insan means al-nas (people), and al-nas includes the disbeliever and the believer, so it is a continuous exception (istithna' muttasil). The reference in ﴿أُولَئِكَ﴾ is to the relative pronoun (al-mawsul) in terms of its being characterised by patience and doing righteous deeds. ﴿لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ﴾ means forgiveness for their sins, and ﴿وَأَجْرٌ كَبِيرٌ﴾ means a reward they will be rewarded with for their good deeds, great and utterly immense.

Then God, glory be to Him, consoled His Messenger ﷺ, saying: ﴿فَلَعَلَّكَ تَارِكٌ بَعْضَ مَا يُوحَى إِلَيْكَ﴾ (p-650), that is: perhaps, because of the enormity of what you see from them of disbelief and denial, and their demanding of signs according to their desires and their obstinacy, you are leaving aside some of what is revealed to you, of what God has sent down to you and commanded you to convey, of what is hard for them to hear or find difficult to act upon, such as reviling their gods and commanding them to believe in God alone.

It has been said: this statement is in the form of a question, that is, "Are you leaving it aside?" It has also been said that it has the meaning of negation with disapproval, that is: "This does not come from you; rather, you convey to them all that God has sent down to you, whether they love it or dislike it, whether they will or refuse."

﴿وَضَائِقٌ بِهِ صَدْرُكَ﴾ is conjoined to تَارِكٌ. The pronoun in بِهِ refers to مَا or to بَعْضَ. He expressed it with ضَائِقٌ rather than ضَيِّقٌ, because the active participle (ism al-fa'il) in it carries the meaning of occurrence and onset, while the adjective in the pattern of the attributive (al-sifah al-mushabbahah) carries the meaning of permanence.

﴿أَنْ يَقُولُوا﴾ means: lest they say, or fearing that they will say, or so that they will not say: ﴿لَوْلَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ كَنْزٌ﴾, that is: why was a treasure not sent down to him, that is, hidden stored wealth from which he could benefit? ﴿أَوْ جَاءَ مَعَهُ مَلَكٌ﴾ means an angel who would confirm him and show us the validity of his message.

Then God, glory be to Him, explained that the state of His Messenger ﷺ is restricted to warning, so He said: ﴿إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ نَذِيرٌ﴾: it is not incumbent upon you except to warn of what has been revealed to you, and it is not incumbent upon you to achieve their demands or to fulfil their proposals. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَكِيلٌ﴾ means He preserves what they say, and He does with them what must be done.

His saying: ﴿أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَرَاهُ﴾: أَمْ here is the disjunctive أَمْ (al-munqati'ah) which has the meaning of بَلْ together with the interrogative hamzah. It turns away from what came before of their negligence toward the revelation and their not being content with what he brought of the clear miracles, and begins to mention their committing what is worse than that, namely their accusation against him that he invented it. The interrogation is for rebuke and reproach. The hidden pronoun in افْتَرَاهُ refers to the Prophet ﷺ, and the explicit pronoun refers to what is revealed.

Then God, glory be to Him, commanded him to answer them with what will silence them, expose their lies and manifest their incapacity, so He said: ﴿قُلْ فَأْتُوا بِعَشْرِ سُوَرٍ مِثْلِهِ﴾, that is, similar to it in eloquence, excellence of arrangement, solidity of wording and grandeur of meanings. He described the surahs with what is used to describe the singular, saying مِثْلَهُنَّ and not أَمْثَالَهُ, because the intended meaning is the similarity of each one of the surahs, or for the purpose of indicating the aspect of resemblance, the basis of which is similarity in one thing, namely eloquence reaching the limit of inimitability. This is only so according to the view that agreement in the plural, dual and singular is a condition.

Then He described the surahs with another attribute, saying: ﴿مُفْتَرَيَاتٍ﴾ (invented). ﴿وَادْعُوا﴾ (and call upon) is for the purpose of seeking aid in the challenge with the ten surahs. ﴿مَنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ﴾ means whoever you are able to call upon and are capable of seeking help from of this human species, and from those you worship and make partners with God, glory be to Him.

His saying: ﴿مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ is connected to ادْعُوا: that is, call upon whomever you can, passing beyond God, the Exalted. ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ means in what you claim of my having invented it.

﴿فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا لَكُمْ﴾: that is, if they do not do what you asked of them and what you challenged them with, namely bringing ten similar surahs, and they do not respond to the required counter-challenge. The pronoun in لَكُمْ may refer to the Messenger of God ﷺ and the believers, or to the Prophet ﷺ alone, in the plural form out of glorification and majesty. ﴿فَاعْلَمُوا﴾ is a command addressed to the Messenger of God ﷺ and the believers, or to the Messenger alone according to the interpretation mentioned shortly before.

The meaning of commanding them with knowledge is commanding them to remain steadfast in it, since they already know this before the disbelievers' incapacity to bring ten similar surahs. Or the intended meaning of the command with knowledge is the command to increase in it, to a degree that no doubt mixes with it and no uncertainty pervades it, which is certainty of knowledge (ilm al-yaqin). The first is preferable.

The meaning of ﴿أَنَّمَا أُنْزِلَ بِعِلْمِ اللَّهِ﴾ is that it was sent down accompanied by the knowledge of God, which is specific to Him, whose reality minds cannot grasp and whose meaning intellects cannot clarify, because of the inimitability it contains, which lies beyond human capacity. ﴿وَأَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ﴾ means: and know that God is the one singular in divinity, with no partner, and no one other than Him can do what He can do.

Then He concluded the verse with His saying: ﴿فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾, that is: will you be steadfast in Islam, sincere toward it, increasing in acts of obedience? Because you have obtained, through the disbelievers' incapacity to produce the like of ten surahs of this Book, a tranquillity beyond what you were upon and an additional insight. And even if you were Muslims before this, steadfastness in it, increase of insight in it and tranquillity through it are demanded of you.

It has been said that the pronoun in ﴿فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا﴾ refers to the relative pronoun in ﴿مَنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ﴾, and the pronoun in لَكُمْ refers to the disbelievers whom the Messenger of God challenged, and likewise the pronoun in فَاعْلَمُوا.

The meaning is: if those whom you called upon to support and assist you in producing ten surahs, from among the rest of the disbelievers and those whom they worship, and who claim that they can harm and benefit, do not respond to you, then know that this Qur'an which God has sent down upon this Messenger is beyond the power of anyone other than Him, glory be to Him and exalted, because of the inimitability it contains, which the strength of created beings falls short of. And know that it was sent down with the knowledge of God, which no minds encompass and no understandings reach. And know that He alone is singular in divinity, with no partner. ﴿فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ بَعْدَ هَذَا مُسْلِمُونَ﴾? That is: will you, after this, enter into Islam, follow its rulings and be guided by its laws?

This interpretation is stronger than the first in one respect and weaker in another. Its strength lies in the coherence of the pronouns, their harmony, and the absence of any need for some of them to be interpreted. Its weakness lies in the fact that the ordering of the command to know upon the non-response of those they called upon and sought help from is somewhat obscure and requires strained interpretation, namely that the non-response of those whom they called upon and sought help from, from among the disbelievers and the idols, despite their eagerness for their support, their backing, their exertion for their not believing, and their persistence in disbelief, indicates that these disbelievers come to know that this Qur'an is from God, and that God, glory be to Him, is the sole God with no partner, and this necessitates their entry into Islam.

Know that the challenge to the disbelievers to counter the Qur'an has varied. At times it was made with the whole Qur'an, as in His saying: ﴿قُلْ لَئِنِ اجْتَمَعَتِ الْإِنْسُ وَالْجِنُّ عَلَى أَنْ يَأْتُوا بِمِثْلِ هَذَا الْقُرْآنِ لَا يَأْتُونَ بِمِثْلِهِ﴾ [al-Isra' 17:88], and at times with ten surahs as in this verse, because ten is the first of the units of counting, and at times with a single surah, as has been mentioned previously, because a surah is the smallest portion of it.

Then God, glory be to Him, threatened whoever has a mind restricted to this world, who seeks nothing else and desires nothing beyond it, saying: ﴿مَنْ كَانَ يُرِيدُ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا وَزِينَتَهَا نُوَفِّ إِلَيْهِمْ أَعْمَالَهُمْ فِيهَا﴾.

Al-Farra' said: كَانَ here is superfluous (za'idah), and for this reason the answer is in the jussive (juzima al-jawab).

Al-Zajjaj said: مَنْ in كَانَ is in a position of jazm as a conditional particle, and its answer is نُوَفِّ إِلَيْهِمْ, that is: whoever wills (man yakun yurid).

The people of tafsir differed regarding this verse. Al-Dahhak said: it was revealed concerning the disbelievers, and al-Nahhas preferred this on the basis of the following verse: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَيْسَ لَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ إِلَّا النَّارُ﴾. It has also been said: the verse is general in application to people, both disbelievers and Muslims.

The meaning is that whoever intends by his deed the portion of this world is rewarded accordingly. By its adornment is meant what embellishes and beautifies it: health, security, abundance of provision, elevation of status, the effectiveness of one's word, and the like.

The inclusion of كَانَ in the verse indicates that they are constantly intending the world by their deeds and hardly intend the Hereafter. For this reason it has been said that, despite being given their portion of this world, they will be punished in the Hereafter, because they have restricted their intention to this world and did not act for the Hereafter.

The apparent meaning of His saying ﴿نُوَفِّ إِلَيْهِمْ أَعْمَالَهُمْ فِيهَا﴾ is that whoever intends his deed for this world will receive the worldly recompense without doubt. But what actually occurs in reality contradicts this, for not every person who desires attains his wish from this world even if he works for it and intends it. Therefore this must be restricted by the will of God, glory be to Him.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 11, verses 13–17 (part 2 of 2):

Al-Qurtubi said: Most scholars hold that this verse is unrestricted (muṭlaq), and so is the verse in al-Shura: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of this world, We will give him of it﴾ [al-Shura: 20], and likewise ﴿Whoever desires the reward of this world, then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter﴾ [al-Nisa': 134]. The verse in Subhan, ﴿Whoever desires the hasty (life), We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We wish﴾ [al-Isra': 18], restricts and explains these verses. His saying, ﴿and therein they will not be deprived﴾, means: these who desire by their deeds the life of this world, therein, that is, in this world, they will not be deprived, that is, they will not be given less of their recompense in it according to their deeds for it. This is generally the case but is not invariable; rather, it applies if His Will, glorified is He, so decrees, and His perfect wisdom favours it.

Al-Qadi said: The meaning of the verse is: whoever, by doing good, intends the life of this world and its adornment, We will pay them their deeds in full, complete, without deficiency in this world, which is what they receive of health, sufficiency, and all other pleasures and benefits. Thus the recompense is specified with what he mentioned, and it is granted to every worker for this world, even if it is little and slight.

His saying, ﴿Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter except the Fire﴾: the reference is to the aforementioned seekers. It is necessary to restrict this to those who did not intend the Hereafter by any of the deeds that count and that merit a good recompense in the abode of the Hereafter; or the verse may be specific to the disbelievers, as was mentioned earlier. ﴿And what they did is rendered void﴾, meaning: there became manifest in the Hereafter the nullification of what they did of deeds whose form was the form of acts of obedience that merit the otherworldly recompense, had they not corrupted them through corruption of their intentions, lack of sincerity, and desiring what is with Allah in the abode of recompense, but restricting that to this world and its adornment. Then Allah, glorified is He, judged their deeds as void, saying: ﴿and vain is what they used to do﴾, that is, their deed was in itself vain and not counted, because it was not done for a valid purpose that merits recompense, and what follows from a valid deed does not follow from it.

His saying, ﴿Is one who is upon a clear proof from his Lord﴾: Allah, glorified is He, made clear that there is a vast difference and a great disparity between one who seeks only this world and one who seeks the Hereafter. The meaning is: Is one who is upon a clear proof from his Lord, in following the Prophet (ﷺ) and in faith in Allah, like others who desire the life of this world and its adornment? It has also been said that what is meant by "one who is upon a clear proof from his Lord" is the Prophet (ﷺ), that is: Is one who has with him a clear evidence from Allah and a miracle, like the Qur'an, and has with him a witness like Jibril, and whom the earlier scriptures foretold, like one who desires the life of this world and its adornment?

The meaning of bayyinah (clear proof) is the argument that indicates the truth. The pronoun in His saying ﴿and a witness recites it﴾ refers to the bayyinah, considering its interpretation as argument. The pronoun in ﴿from Him﴾ refers either to the Qur'an, since it was mentioned earlier in His saying ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"﴾, or it refers to Allah, exalted is He.

The meaning is: and there follows the proof, which is the bayyinah, a witness who testifies to its truth from the Qur'an, or from Allah, glorified is He.

The witness (shahid) is the inimitability (i'jaz) that exists in the Qur'an, or the miracles that appeared to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for these are among the witnesses that accompany the Qur'an.

Al-Farra' said: Some have said: ﴿and a witness recites it, from Him﴾ is the Gospel. Even though it came before, it recites the Qur'an in confirmation. The pronoun in ﴿from Him﴾ refers to Allah, mighty and majestic is He. It has also been said that what is meant by ﴿one who is upon a clear proof from his Lord﴾ is the believers among the People of the Book, such as Abd Allah ibn Salam and his like.

His saying, ﴿and before it was the Book of Musa﴾, is conjoined to "witness," and the implied sense is: and there recites the witness another witness, from before it, which is the Book of Musa. Though it preceded in revelation, it recites the witness in testimony. He placed the witness before the Book of Musa, though the latter is earlier in existence, because the witness is a constant, inseparable attribute, so it is more firmly an attribute than the Book of Musa.

The meaning of the testimony of the Book of Musa, which is the Torah, is that it gave good tidings of Muhammad (ﷺ) and informed that he is a Messenger from Allah.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: and there recites it, from before it, the Book of Musa, because the Prophet (ﷺ) is described in the Book of Musa; they find him written with them in the Torah and the Gospel.

Abu Hatim related from some of them that he recited ﴿and before it the Book of Musa﴾ with a fatha (naṣb), and al-Mahdawi related it from al-Kalbi. Then it is conjoined to the pronoun in "yatluhu" (recites it). The meaning is: Jibril recites the Book of Musa. The accusative of ﴿imaman wa-rahmah﴾ (as a leader and a mercy) is in the sense of a circumstantial state (ḥāl).

Imam: the one who is followed and taken as a model in religion. Rahmah (mercy): the great blessing which Allah bestowed upon those to whom it was sent and upon those after them, in respect of the legal rulings it contains which agree with the ruling of the Qur'an.

The indication in His saying ﴿those﴾ refers to those characterized by that virtuous attribute, which is being upon a clear proof from Allah. The demonstrative is the subject and its predicate is ﴿believe in it﴾, that is, they affirm the Prophet (ﷺ) or the Qur'an. ﴿And whoever disbelieves in it among the factions﴾, that is, in the Prophet or in the Qur'an.

The factions (al-ahzab) are those who banded together against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), from the people of Makkah and others, or those who banded together from among the adherents of all religions. ﴿Then the Fire is his promised place﴾: that is, he is certainly among the people of the Fire. In making the Fire a "promised place" there is an indication that in it are kinds of torment that description cannot encompass. Similar is the saying of Hassan:

You brought them to the watering-places of death, while burning, so the Fire is their promised place, and death is meeting them.

﴿So do not be in doubt about it﴾, that is, do not be in doubt about the Qur'an. In this there is an implicit address to others than the Prophet (ﷺ), since he is protected from doubt about the Qur'an, (p-652) or the phrase refers to the promised place. ﴿Indeed it is the truth from your Lord﴾, so there is no room for doubt about it in any state whatsoever. ﴿But most of the people do not believe﴾ in that, despite the obligation of belief in it and the manifestation of the proofs that necessitate it. They are obstinate while knowing it is the truth, or their hearts have been sealed, so they do not understand that it is the truth at all.

Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿Then are you Muslims?﴾, that he said: it is addressed to the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Anas, regarding His saying ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment﴾, that he said: it was revealed concerning the Jews and the Christians.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abd Allah ibn Ma'bad, who said: A man stood up before Ali and said: "Inform us about this verse: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world﴾ up to His saying ﴿and vain is what they used to do.﴾" He said: "Woe to you! That refers to one who desires only this world and does not desire the Hereafter."

Al-Nahhas narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world﴾, that is, its reward and its adornment, its wealth: ﴿We will pay them﴾, that is, We will give them in full, with health, joy in family, wealth, and children; ﴿and therein they will not be deprived﴾, not be diminished. Then it was abrogated (naskh), by His saying ﴿Whoever desires the hasty (life), We hasten for him therein what We will﴾ [al-Isra': 18], the verse.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated the like of this from al-Suddi.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse that he said: whoever does a righteous deed seeking worldly gain, whether fasting, prayer, or night vigil, and does it only to seek the world, Allah says: "We will pay the one who sought in the world what he did, and his deed is nullified, and he, in the Hereafter, is among the losers."

Ibn Jarir narrated from al-Dahhak, who said: This verse was revealed concerning the people of polytheism.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿We will pay them their deeds﴾, that he said: their good things.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated the like of this from Ibn Jurayj.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿and what they did therein is rendered void﴾, that he said: what they did of good was nullified and became void in the Hereafter; for them there is no recompense therein.

Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid regarding the verse, that he said: they are the people of riya' (showing off).

Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu'aym in al-Ma'rifah narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: There is not a man of Quraysh but that a portion of the Qur'an was revealed concerning him. A man said to him: "What was revealed concerning you?" He said: "Have you not read the surah of Hud: ﴿Is one who is upon a clear proof from his Lord and a witness recites it from Him﴾? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the clear proof from his Lord, and I am the witness from Him."

Ibn Asakir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from another route from him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿Is one who is upon a clear proof from his Lord﴾: I; ﴿and a witness recites it from Him﴾: Ali."

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Abu al-Aliyah regarding His saying ﴿Is one who is upon a clear proof from his Lord﴾, that he said: that is Muhammad (ﷺ).

Abu al-Shaykh narrated the like of this from Ibrahim.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: I said to my father: "People claim, regarding Allah's saying ﴿and a witness recites it from Him﴾, that you are the reciter." He said: "I wish I were he, but it is the tongue of Muhammad (ﷺ)."

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that the witness is Jibril. Sa'id ibn Jubayr agreed with him.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through several routes from Ibn Abbas, who said: Jibril is the witness from Allah concerning what he recites of the Book of Allah which was revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And before it the Book of Musa﴾: he said: before it was the Torah upon the tongue of Musa, just as he recited the Qur'an upon the tongue of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Asakir narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali, regarding His saying ﴿and a witness recites it from Him﴾, that he said: Muhammad is the witness from Allah.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿and before it the Book of Musa﴾, that he said: before it the Book came to Musa.

Abd al-Razzaq and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah regarding ﴿and whoever disbelieves in it among the factions﴾, that he said: the disbelievers are factions, all of them upon disbelief.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah, who said: regarding ﴿and whoever disbelieves in it among the factions﴾: from among the Jews and the Christians.

The lam in ﴿وَلَئِنْ أَذَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ﴾ is the lam introducing an oath (al-lam al-muwatti'a lil-qasam). Al-insan is the genus, so it includes both the believer and the disbeliever. The exception in ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا﴾ indicates this. It has also been said that the intended meaning is the genus of disbelievers. This is supported by the fact that despair, ingratitude, exultation and boasting are, for the most part, the attributes of the people of disbelief, not of the people of Islam. It has also been said that the intended person is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, and it has been said that he is Abdullah ibn Umayya al-Makhzumi.

By mercy here is meant blessing: abundant provision, health, and safety from trials. ﴿ثُمَّ نَزَعْنَاهَا مِنْهُ﴾ means that We take it away from him. ﴿إِنَّهُ لَيَئُوسٌ﴾ means he is despairing of mercy, greatly hopeless of its return and of the like of it. ﴿كَفُورٌ﴾ means one who is greatly ungrateful, and it is denial of it (al-juhud biha), as Ibn al-A'rabi said. The use of the two intensive forms (sigha al-mubalagha) in ﴿لَيَئُوسٌ كَفُورٌ﴾ indicates that man is greatly prone to despair and greatly prone to denial when God takes away some of his blessings. So he does not hope for their return, and he does not give thanks for what he previously had of them.

The use of the word "taste" (al-dhawq) indicates that this behaviour occurs in him when even the least blessing that God bestows upon him is taken away, because tasting (al-idhaqa wa-l-dhawq) is the least by which taste is perceived.

Al-na'ma' is a favour whose effect appears upon its recipient, and al-darra' is the appearance of the effect of harm upon the one afflicted by it.

The meaning is: if God, glory be to Him, makes His servant taste His favour of health, safety and wealth, after he had been in hardship, whether poverty, sickness or fear, he does not respond to that with the gratitude that befits him toward God, glory be to Him. Rather, he says: ﴿ذَهَبَ السَّيِّئَاتُ عَنِّي﴾, that is, the calamities which had troubled him, of hardship, poverty, fear and sickness, have gone away from him and their effect has ceased, while he is not thankful to God nor praising Him for His blessings. ﴿إِنَّهُ لَفَرِحٌ فَخُورٌ﴾ means greatly joyful in insolence and arrogance, greatly boastful toward people and haughty over them because of the blessings with which God has favoured him. The expression of the harm reaching him by the word "touch" (al-mass) is appropriate to the expression of favour by "tasting" (al-idhaqa), since both refer to the least thing to which the term "encounter" (al-mulaqah) can apply, as has been mentioned previously.

﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا﴾: for their custom is patience when trials descend, and gratitude when blessings are received.

Al-Akhfash said: this is an exception that is not from the first part; that is, "but those who are patient and do righteous deeds during both states of blessing and affliction."

Al-Farra' said: it is an exception from the subject of ﴿لَئِنْ أَذَقْنَاهُ﴾, that is, from al-insan, since al-insan means al-nas (people), and al-nas includes the disbeliever and the believer, so it is a continuous exception (istithna' muttasil). The reference in ﴿أُولَئِكَ﴾ is to the relative pronoun (al-mawsul) in terms of its being characterised by patience and doing righteous deeds. ﴿لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ﴾ means forgiveness for their sins, and ﴿وَأَجْرٌ كَبِيرٌ﴾ means a reward they will be rewarded with for their good deeds, great and utterly immense.

Then God, glory be to Him, consoled His Messenger ﷺ, saying: ﴿فَلَعَلَّكَ تَارِكٌ بَعْضَ مَا يُوحَى إِلَيْكَ﴾ (p-650), that is: perhaps, because of the enormity of what you see from them of disbelief and denial, and their demanding of signs according to their desires and their obstinacy, you are leaving aside some of what is revealed to you, of what God has sent down to you and commanded you to convey, of what is hard for them to hear or find difficult to act upon, such as reviling their gods and commanding them to believe in God alone.

It has been said: this statement is in the form of a question, that is, "Are you leaving it aside?" It has also been said that it has the meaning of negation with disapproval, that is: "This does not come from you; rather, you convey to them all that God has sent down to you, whether they love it or dislike it, whether they will or refuse."

﴿وَضَائِقٌ بِهِ صَدْرُكَ﴾ is conjoined to تَارِكٌ. The pronoun in بِهِ refers to مَا or to بَعْضَ. He expressed it with ضَائِقٌ rather than ضَيِّقٌ, because the active participle (ism al-fa'il) in it carries the meaning of occurrence and onset, while the adjective in the pattern of the attributive (al-sifah al-mushabbahah) carries the meaning of permanence.

﴿أَنْ يَقُولُوا﴾ means: lest they say, or fearing that they will say, or so that they will not say: ﴿لَوْلَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ كَنْزٌ﴾, that is: why was a treasure not sent down to him, that is, hidden stored wealth from which he could benefit? ﴿أَوْ جَاءَ مَعَهُ مَلَكٌ﴾ means an angel who would confirm him and show us the validity of his message.

Then God, glory be to Him, explained that the state of His Messenger ﷺ is restricted to warning, so He said: ﴿إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ نَذِيرٌ﴾: it is not incumbent upon you except to warn of what has been revealed to you, and it is not incumbent upon you to achieve their demands or to fulfil their proposals. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَكِيلٌ﴾ means He preserves what they say, and He does with them what must be done.

His saying: ﴿أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَرَاهُ﴾: أَمْ here is the disjunctive أَمْ (al-munqati'ah) which has the meaning of بَلْ together with the interrogative hamzah. It turns away from what came before of their negligence toward the revelation and their not being content with what he brought of the clear miracles, and begins to mention their committing what is worse than that, namely their accusation against him that he invented it. The interrogation is for rebuke and reproach. The hidden pronoun in افْتَرَاهُ refers to the Prophet ﷺ, and the explicit pronoun refers to what is revealed.

Then God, glory be to Him, commanded him to answer them with what will silence them, expose their lies and manifest their incapacity, so He said: ﴿قُلْ فَأْتُوا بِعَشْرِ سُوَرٍ مِثْلِهِ﴾, that is, similar to it in eloquence, excellence of arrangement, solidity of wording and grandeur of meanings. He described the surahs with what is used to describe the singular, saying مِثْلَهُنَّ and not أَمْثَالَهُ, because the intended meaning is the similarity of each one of the surahs, or for the purpose of indicating the aspect of resemblance, the basis of which is similarity in one thing, namely eloquence reaching the limit of inimitability. This is only so according to the view that agreement in the plural, dual and singular is a condition.

Then He described the surahs with another attribute, saying: ﴿مُفْتَرَيَاتٍ﴾ (invented). ﴿وَادْعُوا﴾ (and call upon) is for the purpose of seeking aid in the challenge with the ten surahs. ﴿مَنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ﴾ means whoever you are able to call upon and are capable of seeking help from of this human species, and from those you worship and make partners with God, glory be to Him.

His saying: ﴿مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ is connected to ادْعُوا: that is, call upon whomever you can, passing beyond God, the Exalted. ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ means in what you claim of my having invented it.

﴿فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا لَكُمْ﴾: that is, if they do not do what you asked of them and what you challenged them with, namely bringing ten similar surahs, and they do not respond to the required counter-challenge. The pronoun in لَكُمْ may refer to the Messenger of God ﷺ and the believers, or to the Prophet ﷺ alone, in the plural form out of glorification and majesty. ﴿فَاعْلَمُوا﴾ is a command addressed to the Messenger of God ﷺ and the believers, or to the Messenger alone according to the interpretation mentioned shortly before.

The meaning of commanding them with knowledge is commanding them to remain steadfast in it, since they already know this before the disbelievers' incapacity to bring ten similar surahs. Or the intended meaning of the command with knowledge is the command to increase in it, to a degree that no doubt mixes with it and no uncertainty pervades it, which is certainty of knowledge (ilm al-yaqin). The first is preferable.

The meaning of ﴿أَنَّمَا أُنْزِلَ بِعِلْمِ اللَّهِ﴾ is that it was sent down accompanied by the knowledge of God, which is specific to Him, whose reality minds cannot grasp and whose meaning intellects cannot clarify, because of the inimitability it contains, which lies beyond human capacity. ﴿وَأَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ﴾ means: and know that God is the one singular in divinity, with no partner, and no one other than Him can do what He can do.

Then He concluded the verse with His saying: ﴿فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾, that is: will you be steadfast in Islam, sincere toward it, increasing in acts of obedience? Because you have obtained, through the disbelievers' incapacity to produce the like of ten surahs of this Book, a tranquillity beyond what you were upon and an additional insight. And even if you were Muslims before this, steadfastness in it, increase of insight in it and tranquillity through it are demanded of you.

It has been said that the pronoun in ﴿فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا﴾ refers to the relative pronoun in ﴿مَنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ﴾, and the pronoun in لَكُمْ refers to the disbelievers whom the Messenger of God challenged, and likewise the pronoun in فَاعْلَمُوا.

The meaning is: if those whom you called upon to support and assist you in producing ten surahs, from among the rest of the disbelievers and those whom they worship, and who claim that they can harm and benefit, do not respond to you, then know that this Qur'an which God has sent down upon this Messenger is beyond the power of anyone other than Him, glory be to Him and exalted, because of the inimitability it contains, which the strength of created beings falls short of. And know that it was sent down with the knowledge of God, which no minds encompass and no understandings reach. And know that He alone is singular in divinity, with no partner. ﴿فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ بَعْدَ هَذَا مُسْلِمُونَ﴾? That is: will you, after this, enter into Islam, follow its rulings and be guided by its laws?

This interpretation is stronger than the first in one respect and weaker in another. Its strength lies in the coherence of the pronouns, their harmony, and the absence of any need for some of them to be interpreted. Its weakness lies in the fact that the ordering of the command to know upon the non-response of those they called upon and sought help from is somewhat obscure and requires strained interpretation, namely that the non-response of those whom they called upon and sought help from, from among the disbelievers and the idols, despite their eagerness for their support, their backing, their exertion for their not believing, and their persistence in disbelief, indicates that these disbelievers come to know that this Qur'an is from God, and that God, glory be to Him, is the sole God with no partner, and this necessitates their entry into Islam.

Know that the challenge to the disbelievers to counter the Qur'an has varied. At times it was made with the whole Qur'an, as in His saying: ﴿قُلْ لَئِنِ اجْتَمَعَتِ الْإِنْسُ وَالْجِنُّ عَلَى أَنْ يَأْتُوا بِمِثْلِ هَذَا الْقُرْآنِ لَا يَأْتُونَ بِمِثْلِهِ﴾ [al-Isra' 17:88], and at times with ten surahs as in this verse, because ten is the first of the units of counting, and at times with a single surah, as has been mentioned previously, because a surah is the smallest portion of it.

Then God, glory be to Him, threatened whoever has a mind restricted to this world, who seeks nothing else and desires nothing beyond it, saying: ﴿مَنْ كَانَ يُرِيدُ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا وَزِينَتَهَا نُوَفِّ إِلَيْهِمْ أَعْمَالَهُمْ فِيهَا﴾.

Al-Farra' said: كَانَ here is superfluous (za'idah), and for this reason the answer is in the jussive (juzima al-jawab).

Al-Zajjaj said: مَنْ in كَانَ is in a position of jazm as a conditional particle, and its answer is نُوَفِّ إِلَيْهِمْ, that is: whoever wills (man yakun yurid).

The people of tafsir differed regarding this verse. Al-Dahhak said: it was revealed concerning the disbelievers, and al-Nahhas preferred this on the basis of the following verse: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَيْسَ لَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ إِلَّا النَّارُ﴾. It has also been said: the verse is general in application to people, both disbelievers and Muslims.

The meaning is that whoever intends by his deed the portion of this world is rewarded accordingly. By its adornment is meant what embellishes and beautifies it: health, security, abundance of provision, elevation of status, the effectiveness of one's word, and the like.

The inclusion of كَانَ in the verse indicates that they are constantly intending the world by their deeds and hardly intend the Hereafter. For this reason it has been said that, despite being given their portion of this world, they will be punished in the Hereafter, because they have restricted their intention to this world and did not act for the Hereafter.

The apparent meaning of His saying ﴿نُوَفِّ إِلَيْهِمْ أَعْمَالَهُمْ فِيهَا﴾ is that whoever intends his deed for this world will receive the worldly recompense without doubt. But what actually occurs in reality contradicts this, for not every person who desires attains his wish from this world even if he works for it and intends it. Therefore this must be restricted by the will of God, glory be to Him.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 11, verses 13–17 (part 2 of 2):

Al-Qurtubi said: Most scholars hold that this verse is unrestricted (muṭlaq), and so is the verse in al-Shura: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of this world, We will give him of it﴾ [al-Shura: 20], and likewise ﴿Whoever desires the reward of this world, then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter﴾ [al-Nisa': 134]. The verse in Subhan, ﴿Whoever desires the hasty (life), We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We wish﴾ [al-Isra': 18], restricts and explains these verses. His saying, ﴿and therein they will not be deprived﴾, means: these who desire by their deeds the life of this world, therein, that is, in this world, they will not be deprived, that is, they will not be given less of their recompense in it according to their deeds for it. This is generally the case but is not invariable; rather, it applies if His Will, glorified is He, so decrees, and His perfect wisdom favours it.

Al-Qadi said: The meaning of the verse is: whoever, by doing good, intends the life of this world and its adornment, We will pay them their deeds in full, complete, without deficiency in this world, which is what they receive of health, sufficiency, and all other pleasures and benefits. Thus the recompense is specified with what he mentioned, and it is granted to every worker for this world, even if it is little and slight.

His saying, ﴿Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter except the Fire﴾: the reference is to the aforementioned seekers. It is necessary to restrict this to those who did not intend the Hereafter by any of the deeds that count and that merit a good recompense in the abode of the Hereafter; or the verse may be specific to the disbelievers, as was mentioned earlier. ﴿And what they did is rendered void﴾, meaning: there became manifest in the Hereafter the nullification of what they did of deeds whose form was the form of acts of obedience that merit the otherworldly recompense, had they not corrupted them through corruption of their intentions, lack of sincerity, and desiring what is with Allah in the abode of recompense, but restricting that to this world and its adornment. Then Allah, glorified is He, judged their deeds as void, saying: ﴿and vain is what they used to do﴾, that is, their deed was in itself vain and not counted, because it was not done for a valid purpose that merits recompense, and what follows from a valid deed does not follow from it.

His saying, ﴿Is one who is upon a clear proof from his Lord﴾: Allah, glorified is He, made clear that there is a vast difference and a great disparity between one who seeks only this world and one who seeks the Hereafter. The meaning is: Is one who is upon a clear proof from his Lord, in following the Prophet (ﷺ) and in faith in Allah, like others who desire the life of this world and its adornment? It has also been said that what is meant by "one who is upon a clear proof from his Lord" is the Prophet (ﷺ), that is: Is one who has with him a clear evidence from Allah and a miracle, like the Qur'an, and has with him a witness like Jibril, and whom the earlier scriptures foretold, like one who desires the life of this world and its adornment?

The meaning of bayyinah (clear proof) is the argument that indicates the truth. The pronoun in His saying ﴿and a witness recites it﴾ refers to the bayyinah, considering its interpretation as argument. The pronoun in ﴿from Him﴾ refers either to the Qur'an, since it was mentioned earlier in His saying ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"﴾, or it refers to Allah, exalted is He.

The meaning is: and there follows the proof, which is the bayyinah, a witness who testifies to its truth from the Qur'an, or from Allah, glorified is He.

The witness (shahid) is the inimitability (i'jaz) that exists in the Qur'an, or the miracles that appeared to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for these are among the witnesses that accompany the Qur'an.

Al-Farra' said: Some have said: ﴿and a witness recites it, from Him﴾ is the Gospel. Even though it came before, it recites the Qur'an in confirmation. The pronoun in ﴿from Him﴾ refers to Allah, mighty and majestic is He. It has also been said that what is meant by ﴿one who is upon a clear proof from his Lord﴾ is the believers among the People of the Book, such as Abd Allah ibn Salam and his like.

His saying, ﴿and before it was the Book of Musa﴾, is conjoined to "witness," and the implied sense is: and there recites the witness another witness, from before it, which is the Book of Musa. Though it preceded in revelation, it recites the witness in testimony. He placed the witness before the Book of Musa, though the latter is earlier in existence, because the witness is a constant, inseparable attribute, so it is more firmly an attribute than the Book of Musa.

The meaning of the testimony of the Book of Musa, which is the Torah, is that it gave good tidings of Muhammad (ﷺ) and informed that he is a Messenger from Allah.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: and there recites it, from before it, the Book of Musa, because the Prophet (ﷺ) is described in the Book of Musa; they find him written with them in the Torah and the Gospel.

Abu Hatim related from some of them that he recited ﴿and before it the Book of Musa﴾ with a fatha (naṣb), and al-Mahdawi related it from al-Kalbi. Then it is conjoined to the pronoun in "yatluhu" (recites it). The meaning is: Jibril recites the Book of Musa. The accusative of ﴿imaman wa-rahmah﴾ (as a leader and a mercy) is in the sense of a circumstantial state (ḥāl).

Imam: the one who is followed and taken as a model in religion. Rahmah (mercy): the great blessing which Allah bestowed upon those to whom it was sent and upon those after them, in respect of the legal rulings it contains which agree with the ruling of the Qur'an.

The indication in His saying ﴿those﴾ refers to those characterized by that virtuous attribute, which is being upon a clear proof from Allah. The demonstrative is the subject and its predicate is ﴿believe in it﴾, that is, they affirm the Prophet (ﷺ) or the Qur'an. ﴿And whoever disbelieves in it among the factions﴾, that is, in the Prophet or in the Qur'an.

The factions (al-ahzab) are those who banded together against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), from the people of Makkah and others, or those who banded together from among the adherents of all religions. ﴿Then the Fire is his promised place﴾: that is, he is certainly among the people of the Fire. In making the Fire a "promised place" there is an indication that in it are kinds of torment that description cannot encompass. Similar is the saying of Hassan:

You brought them to the watering-places of death, while burning, so the Fire is their promised place, and death is meeting them.

﴿So do not be in doubt about it﴾, that is, do not be in doubt about the Qur'an. In this there is an implicit address to others than the Prophet (ﷺ), since he is protected from doubt about the Qur'an, (p-652) or the phrase refers to the promised place. ﴿Indeed it is the truth from your Lord﴾, so there is no room for doubt about it in any state whatsoever. ﴿But most of the people do not believe﴾ in that, despite the obligation of belief in it and the manifestation of the proofs that necessitate it. They are obstinate while knowing it is the truth, or their hearts have been sealed, so they do not understand that it is the truth at all.

Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿Then are you Muslims?﴾, that he said: it is addressed to the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Anas, regarding His saying ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment﴾, that he said: it was revealed concerning the Jews and the Christians.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abd Allah ibn Ma'bad, who said: A man stood up before Ali and said: "Inform us about this verse: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world﴾ up to His saying ﴿and vain is what they used to do.﴾" He said: "Woe to you! That refers to one who desires only this world and does not desire the Hereafter."

Al-Nahhas narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world﴾, that is, its reward and its adornment, its wealth: ﴿We will pay them﴾, that is, We will give them in full, with health, joy in family, wealth, and children; ﴿and therein they will not be deprived﴾, not be diminished. Then it was abrogated (naskh), by His saying ﴿Whoever desires the hasty (life), We hasten for him therein what We will﴾ [al-Isra': 18], the verse.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated the like of this from al-Suddi.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse that he said: whoever does a righteous deed seeking worldly gain, whether fasting, prayer, or night vigil, and does it only to seek the world, Allah says: "We will pay the one who sought in the world what he did, and his deed is nullified, and he, in the Hereafter, is among the losers."

Ibn Jarir narrated from al-Dahhak, who said: This verse was revealed concerning the people of polytheism.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿We will pay them their deeds﴾, that he said: their good things.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated the like of this from Ibn Jurayj.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿and what they did therein is rendered void﴾, that he said: what they did of good was nullified and became void in the Hereafter; for them there is no recompense therein.

Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid regarding the verse, that he said: they are the people of riya' (showing off).

Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu'aym in al-Ma'rifah narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: There is not a man of Quraysh but that a portion of the Qur'an was revealed concerning him. A man said to him: "What was revealed concerning you?" He said: "Have you not read the surah of Hud: ﴿Is one who is upon a clear proof from his Lord and a witness recites it from Him﴾? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the clear proof from his Lord, and I am the witness from Him."

Ibn Asakir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from another route from him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿Is one who is upon a clear proof from his Lord﴾: I; ﴿and a witness recites it from Him﴾: Ali."

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Abu al-Aliyah regarding His saying ﴿Is one who is upon a clear proof from his Lord﴾, that he said: that is Muhammad (ﷺ).

Abu al-Shaykh narrated the like of this from Ibrahim.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: I said to my father: "People claim, regarding Allah's saying ﴿and a witness recites it from Him﴾, that you are the reciter." He said: "I wish I were he, but it is the tongue of Muhammad (ﷺ)."

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that the witness is Jibril. Sa'id ibn Jubayr agreed with him.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through several routes from Ibn Abbas, who said: Jibril is the witness from Allah concerning what he recites of the Book of Allah which was revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And before it the Book of Musa﴾: he said: before it was the Torah upon the tongue of Musa, just as he recited the Qur'an upon the tongue of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Asakir narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali, regarding His saying ﴿and a witness recites it from Him﴾, that he said: Muhammad is the witness from Allah.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿and before it the Book of Musa﴾, that he said: before it the Book came to Musa.

Abd al-Razzaq and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah regarding ﴿and whoever disbelieves in it among the factions﴾, that he said: the disbelievers are factions, all of them upon disbelief.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah, who said: regarding ﴿and whoever disbelieves in it among the factions﴾: from among the Jews and the Christians.

The lam in ﴿وَلَئِنْ أَذَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ﴾ is the lam introducing an oath (al-lam al-muwatti'a lil-qasam). Al-insan is the genus, so it includes both the believer and the disbeliever. The exception in ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا﴾ indicates this. It has also been said that the intended meaning is the genus of disbelievers. This is supported by the fact that despair, ingratitude, exultation and boasting are, for the most part, the attributes of the people of disbelief, not of the people of Islam. It has also been said that the intended person is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, and it has been said that he is Abdullah ibn Umayya al-Makhzumi.

By mercy here is meant blessing: abundant provision, health, and safety from trials. ﴿ثُمَّ نَزَعْنَاهَا مِنْهُ﴾ means that We take it away from him. ﴿إِنَّهُ لَيَئُوسٌ﴾ means he is despairing of mercy, greatly hopeless of its return and of the like of it. ﴿كَفُورٌ﴾ means one who is greatly ungrateful, and it is denial of it (al-juhud biha), as Ibn al-A'rabi said. The use of the two intensive forms (sigha al-mubalagha) in ﴿لَيَئُوسٌ كَفُورٌ﴾ indicates that man is greatly prone to despair and greatly prone to denial when God takes away some of his blessings. So he does not hope for their return, and he does not give thanks for what he previously had of them.
