As for the fatḥa, by the first possibility, it is what we have mentioned. The second possibility: the alif is deleted due to the meeting of two unvocalized letters (iltiqāʾ al-sākinayn).

As for the kasra, the first possibility is as we have mentioned, and the second is that it is deleted due to the meeting of two unvocalized letters. Thus al-Naḥḥās related it from him.

Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī and Ḥafṣ recited ﴿Board with us﴾ with the assimilation (idghām) of the bāʾ into the mīm, because the two are close in their point of articulation.

The rest recited without assimilation.

﴿And be not with the disbelievers﴾. He forbade him from being with the disbelievers, that is, outside the ship. It is possible that being with them is meant as being upon their religion.

Then God, glorified is He, related what Noah's son answered his father, so He said: ﴿He said, "I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water."﴾ That is, it will prevent the water from reaching me by its height. Noah answered him with his words: ﴿There is no protector today from the decree of God﴾, that is, there is no preventer, for it is a day upon which the punishment has become due and the pen has dried concerning what is to occur in it. He negated the genus of the protector, so the protector from drowning on that day is included under it in the first instance. He expressed the water, or the drowning, as "the decree of God" to magnify its matter and to make its affair terrifying.

As for the exception, al-Zajjāj said: it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), meaning: but whoever God has mercy upon, He protects him. So ﴿whom He has mercy upon﴾ is in the accusative position. It is permissible for the exception to be connected (muttaṣil), with "protector" meaning "one protected": that is, there is no one protected today from the decree of God except whom God has had mercy upon, like ﴿a gushing fluid﴾ [al-Ṭāriq: 6] and ﴿a pleasant life﴾ [al-Ḥāqqah: 21]. From this is the saying of the poet:

"Leave off nobility, do not rise to seek it,
and sit, for you are the one fed and clothed."

That is, the one fed and the one clothed. Ibn Jarīr chose this possibility. It was also said: "protector" means "one possessing protection," like "labin" and "tamir." The meaning is: there is no protector at all except in the place of whom God has had mercy upon, and that is the ship. In that case, there is no objection raised that says: the meaning of "whom He has had mercy upon" is "whom God has had mercy upon," and whom God has had mercy upon is protected, so how can his exception from the protector be valid? Because in each of these possibilities there is a removal of the problem.

It was also recited as "illā man rūḥima" (except whom He has had mercy upon) in the passive voice.

﴿And the wave came between them﴾, that is, it came between Noah and his son, so his escape from drowning became impossible. It was also said: between Noah's son and the mountain. The first is preferable, because the consequence ﴿so he was among the drowned﴾ that follows it indicates the first and not the second, since the mountain does not protect.

God said: ﴿And it was said, "O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold."﴾ It is said: "balaʿa al-māʾ yabluʿuhu" like "manaʿa yamnaʿu," and "baliʿa yableʿu" like "ḥamida yaḥmadu," two dialects related by al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ. And "al-balʿ" is drinking, and from it comes "al-bālūʿa," which is the place that drinks the water. And "al-izdirād" (swallowing). It is said: "balaʿa mā fī famihi min al-ṭaʿām" when he swallowed what was in his mouth of food. The verb "balʿ," which is an action of animals, was borrowed for absorption, indicating that this is not like the usual absorption that occurs gradually.

﴿And O sky, withhold.﴾ "Al-iqlāʿ" is withholding. It is said: "aqlaʿa al-maṭar" when the rain stopped.

The meaning is: He commanded the sky to withhold the water from being sent down. He placed the call to the earth before the sky because the beginning of the flood was from it.

﴿And the water subsided﴾, that is, decreased. It is said: "ghāḍa al-māʾ" and "ghuḍtuhu anā" (I caused it to subside).

﴿And the matter was decided﴾, that is, it was made firm and completed. He means: God destroyed the people of Noah in completeness and firmness.

﴿And it came to rest upon al-Jūdī﴾, that is, the ship settled upon the well-known mountain called al-Jūdī, which is a mountain near Mosul. It was also said: al-Jūdī is the name of every mountain. From this is the saying of Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl:

"Glory be to Him, then glory, we seek refuge in Him,
and before us, al-Jūdī and the rocks glorified Him."

It is said that it is from the mountains of Paradise, which is why the ship settled upon it.

﴿And it was said, "Away with the wrongdoing people."﴾ The speaker is God, glorified is He, to match the beginning of the verse. It was also said: it is Noah and his companions.

The meaning: and it was said, "Ruin for the wrongdoing people." This is one of the expressions specific to supplications of evil. He described them with wrongdoing to indicate that it is the cause of the destruction, and to allude to His saying: ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged﴾ [Hūd: 37].

The scholars of rhetoric have agreed that this noble verse reaches such a degree of eloquence and rhetoric that description falls short of it, and the capacity of those capable of the arts of rhetoric, firmly established in the science of eloquence, deeply rooted in the science of language, acquainted with what has been recorded from the sermons of the most eloquent orators of the Arabs and the poems of their most outstanding poets, and trained in the subtleties of the sciences and secrets of Arabic, is too weak to produce anything close to it.

A group of them has addressed the explanation of some of what it includes of this, and they were lengthy and excellent. May God have mercy upon us and them with His vast mercy.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Qatādah concerning His saying: ﴿then upon me is my crime﴾, he said: "my deed." ﴿And I am innocent of what you commit﴾, that is, of what you do.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from Qatādah concerning His saying: ﴿And it was revealed to Noah that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾, and that was when Noah invoked against them, and he said: ﴿My Lord, leave not upon the earth from among the disbelievers a dweller﴾ [Nuh: 26].

Aḥmad in al-Zuhd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abū al-Shaykh related from al-Ḥasan, who said: Noah did not invoke against his people until this verse was revealed, so his hope in them was cut off at that point, and he invoked against them.

Ibn Jarīr related from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying: ﴿So do not be distressed﴾, he said: "so do not grieve."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqī related from him concerning His saying: ﴿And construct the ship under Our eyes and Our revelation﴾, he said: "under God's eye and His revelation."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from him also, he said: Noah did not know how to build the ship, so God revealed to him to build it like the breast of a bird (jujuʾ al-ṭāʾir).

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh, al-Ḥākim and Ibn Mardawayh related from ʿĀʾishah, she said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Noah remained among his people for a thousand years less fifty years, calling them. Until, at the end of his time, he planted a tree, and it grew tall and spread in every direction. Then he cut it and began to shape it into a ship, and people would pass by and ask him, and he would say, 'I am making it into a ship.' They would mock him and say, 'He is making a ship on dry land! How will it sail?' He said, 'You will soon know.' When he finished it, and the oven gushed forth, and water increased in the lanes, the mother of the boy feared for him, for she loved him intensely. So she went out to the mountain until she reached a third of it. When the water reached her, she went up until she stood upon the mountain. When the water reached his neck, she lifted him before her until the water carried them off. Had God had mercy upon anyone among them, He would have had mercy upon the mother of the boy."

Al-Dhahabī criticized it in his addition to al-Ḥākim's Mustadrak.

Narrations and reports have been related concerning the description of the ship and its dimensions, but mentioning them here has little benefit.

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying: ﴿upon whom will come a punishment that disgraces him﴾, he said: "it is drowning." ﴿And there will descend upon him a lasting punishment﴾, he said: "it is abiding in the Fire."

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh and al-Ḥākim, who authenticated it, related from him: between the call of Noah and the destruction of his people there were three hundred years, and the oven gushed forth in India, and Noah's ship circled the House (of God) seven times.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim also related from him: "al-tannūr" is the spring in the island, the spring of al-Warda.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, who said: The oven gushed forth from the mosque of Kufa, from the direction of the gates of Kinda.

Similar to this has been related from him through several chains.

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: "al-tannūr" is the surface of the earth. It was said to him: when you see the water on the surface of the earth, board, you and those with you.

The Arabs call the surface of the earth "tannūr al-arḍ."

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir related from ʿAlī concerning ﴿and the oven gushed forth﴾, he said: "The dawn rose." It was said to him: when the dawn rises, board, you and your companions.

Other interpretations of "al-tannūr" have been related besides this, and we have already mentioned the reference to that.

Numerous narrations have been related concerning the description of the story, what Noah carried in the ship, how the drowning occurred, and how long the ship remained upon the surface of the water. [p. 660] They have no place in the explanation of the speech of God, glorified is He.

Ibn Jarīr related from Mujāhid concerning His saying: ﴿In the name of God is its course and its anchorage﴾, he said: "when they board, and when they set sail, and when they anchor."

Ibn Jarīr related from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, he said: When he wanted it to anchor, he said, "In the name of God," and it anchored; and when he wanted it to sail, he said, "In the name of God," and it sailed.

Abū Yaʿlā, al-Ṭabarānī, Ibn al-Sunnī, Ibn ʿAdī, Abū al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh related from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "A protection for my nation from drowning, when they board the ship, is that they say: 'In the name of God, the King, the Most Merciful, ﴿In the name of God is its course and its anchorage. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾' and ﴿They did not appraise God with the appraisal due to Him﴾ to the end of the verse."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim, al-Ṭabarānī and Ibn Mardawayh related it from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Abū al-Shaykh also related it from him as a marfūʿ report through another route.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Qatādah, he said: The name of Noah's son who drowned was Kanʿān.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: He was his son, except that he opposed him in intention and action.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from ʿIkrimah concerning His saying: ﴿There is no protector today from the decree of God except whom He has mercy upon﴾, he said: "No one is saved except the people of the ship."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from al-Qāsim ibn Abī Barra concerning His saying: ﴿And the wave came between them﴾, he said: "between Noah's son and the mountain."

Ibn al-Mundhir related from ʿIkrimah concerning His saying: ﴿O earth, swallow﴾, he said: "It is in Abyssinian (Ḥabashiyya)."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from Wahb ibn Munabbih concerning "iblaʿī," he said in Abyssinian: that is, "swallow it."

Abū al-Shaykh related from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, he said: Its meaning is "drink," in the language of India.

The Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 11, verses 35–44 (part 3 of 3):

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas the like of it.

I say: The occurrence of the word *al-bal'* (swallowing) and what is derived from it in the language of the Arabs is apparent and manifest, so what concern is it of ours with the Abyssinians and the Indians?

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 11, verses 35–44 (part 1 of 3):

.
His saying: ﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated it"?﴾ He, glorified is He, rebuked them for their saying that what was revealed to Nuh was a fabrication. He said: ﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated it"?﴾ Then He commanded him to respond with a fair statement, and said: ﴿Say: If I have fabricated it, upon me is my crime.﴾ With a kasra on the hamza, according to the recitation of the majority (qira'a, a recitational reading), it is a verbal noun from ajrama, meaning to commit what entails sin. Jarama and ajrama have the same meaning, as al-Nahhas said. The meaning is: upon me is my sin, or the recompense of my earning.
Whoever reads it with a fatha on the hamza says it is a plural. Al-Nahhas mentioned this. ﴿And I am innocent of what you commit (tajrimun)﴾, that is, innocent of your crime, because of what you attribute to me of fabrication. It has been said that there is an ellipsis in the speech, and the sense is: "But I have not fabricated it. So the crime and its punishment are only upon you, and I am innocent of it."
The exegetes differed concerning this verse. It has been said that it is a report about Nuh and what he said to his people. It has also been said that it is a report about the exchange that took place between our Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, and the disbelievers of Makkah.
The first view is preferable, because the speech before and after it is addressed to Nuh, peace be upon him.
His saying: ﴿And it was revealed to Nuh: "None of your people will believe except those who have already believed."﴾ The phrase "that he will not believe" is in the nominative position, as the deputy of the unnamed subject (na'ib al-fa'il).
It may also be in the accusative position, with the preposition bi- understood, meaning "that he..." The speech contains a discouragement for him regarding their faith: they persist in their disbelief, are determined upon it, and none of them will believe except those whose faith has already preceded. ﴿So do not grieve (tabta'is) over what they have been doing.﴾ Al-bu's means sorrow, that is, do not grieve. Al-ba'is means the one who is humbled. So Allah, glorified is He, forbade him from grieving the grief of one who is humbled, because ibti'as is grief accompanied by submission.
From this is the saying of the poet:
How many a friend or intimate have I lost, yet I did not grieve, though the loss in it is great.
Then, when Allah, glorified is He, informed him that they would never believe, He made him know the manner of their destruction, and inspired him with the matter by which he and those who believed with him would be saved. He said: ﴿And construct the ark under Our eyes and Our inspiration.﴾ That is: make the ship, while under Our eyes, that is, in Our sight. The intended meaning is Our protection and Our guarding of you. He expressed this by "eyes" because they are the instrument of sight, and sight is generally that by which protection and guarding occur. The plural "eyes" is used for magnification, not for multiplicity. It has been said that the meaning is "under Our eyes" meaning under the eyes of Our angels whom We made as eyes over your protection. It has been said: "under Our eyes" means with Our knowledge, and it has been said: by Our command.
The meaning of "by Our inspiration" is by what We revealed to you of the manner of its construction. ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have done wrong﴾, that is, do not request their respite, for the time of retribution against them has come. The clause ﴿indeed they are to be drowned﴾ is explanatory: that is, do not ask Us to delay them, for they are judged by Us to be drowned, and the decree has already passed, so there is no way to repel it or postpone it. It has been said: the meaning is, do not address Me about hastening their punishment, for they will be drowned at the appointed time for that, and their drowning will not be delayed beyond it. It has also been said: the intended "those who have done wrong" are his wife and his son.
﴿And he began constructing the ark﴾, that is, he began to make the ship, or he took up making the ship. It has been said that this is a report of a past state in order to bring the scene to mind. The clause ﴿and whenever a group of his people passed by him, they mocked him﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal), that is, they ridiculed him for building the ship.
Al-Akhfash and al-Kisa'i said: it is said "sakhira bihi" and "sakhira minhu."
Regarding the manner of their mockery of him, there are two views. The first is that they would see him building the ship and say: "O Nuh, after prophethood you have become a carpenter!" The second is that when they saw him building the ship, and they did not know it before that, they said: "O Nuh, what are you making?" He said: "I will sail it upon the water." So they marveled at his statement and mocked him.
Then he answered them with his saying: ﴿If you mock us, then we will mock you as you mock.﴾ This statement is resumptive, as if answering an implied question, as if it were said: "What did he say to them?" The meaning is: if you mock us today for our building of the ship, then we will mock you tomorrow at the time of drowning.
The meaning of mockery here is making them appear foolish: that is, if you make us look foolish, then we will make you look foolish as you do. His making them look foolish is with regard to his displaying it to them and addressing them directly; otherwise they were foolish before this and after it. The comparison in His saying ﴿as you mock﴾ is either for mere certainty and occurrence, or for renewal and repetition. The meaning is: we will mock you with a certain and actual mockery, just as you mock us, or with a renewed and repeated mockery, just as you mock us. It has also been said the meaning is: we will mock you in the future with a mockery like your mockery when the drowning overtakes you. There is a point to consider here, for their state at that time does not suit mockery, since they will be occupied by a preoccupying distress.
Then he threatened them with His saying: ﴿So you will come to know who will receive a punishment that disgraces him﴾. That is the punishment of drowning in this world. ﴿And there will descend upon him a lasting punishment﴾. That is the constant punishment of the Fire. The meaning of "yahill" (descends) is that it makes what was deferred immediate, derived from the falling due of a deferred debt. "Man" is a relative pronoun in the accusative position. It may also be interrogative in the nominative position, meaning: which of us will receive a punishment that disgraces him. It has also been said: it is in the nominative position as the inchoative, with "ya'tihi" as the predicate, and "yukhzihi" as an attribute of "adhab."
Al-Kisa'i said: some people of the Hijaz say "sawfa ta'lamun," and whoever says "sata'lamun" drops both the waw and the fa'. The Kufans permitted "sawfa ta'lamun," while the Basrans prohibited it. The intended "punishment of disgrace" is the punishment that disgraces its owner, and upon whom shame descends.
His saying: ﴿Until, when Our command came and the oven (tannur) boiled over﴾. "Hatta" here is the inceptive "hatta," which introduces a conditional clause, and it is made the end point (ghaya) of His saying: ﴿and construct the ark under Our eyes﴾.
The tannur has been interpreted in various ways. The first: it is the surface of the earth, and the Arabs call the surface of the earth a tannur. This is reported from Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, al-Zuhri, and Ibn 'Uyaynah.
The second: it is the oven in which they bake bread. This is the view of Mujahid, 'Ata' and al-Hasan, and it is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas.
The third: it is the place where water gathers in the ship. This is reported from al-Hasan.
The fourth: it is the break of dawn, from the expression "tannur al-fajr." This is reported from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib.
The fifth: it is the mosque of Kufah. This is reported from 'Ali as well and from Mujahid. Mujahid said: the tannur was on the side of Kufah.
The sixth: it is the high parts of the earth and the elevated places. This is said by Qatadah.
The seventh: it is the spring located in al-Jazirah called 'Ayn al-Wardah. This is reported from 'Ikrimah.
The eighth: it is a place in India. Ibn 'Abbas said: the tannur of Adam was in India.
Al-Nahhas said: these views are not contradictory, for Allah, glorified is He, has informed that the water came from the sky and the earth. He said: ﴿So We opened the gates of the sky with pouring water, and We caused the earth to burst forth with springs﴾ [al-Qamar 11–12]. So these views converge in that this was a sign. Thus he said. But there is a point to consider here, for the fourth view contradicts this convergence, and the interpretation by the gushing of water does not fit it, unless the intended meaning is merely the sign, as he mentioned at the end.
The lexicographers have mentioned that "fawr" means boiling, and that "tannur" is a foreign word which the Arabs arabicized. It has been said that the meaning of ﴿and the oven boiled over﴾ is an image of the arrival of the punishment, like the saying: "hamiya al-watis," meaning the battle became fierce. From this is the saying of the poet:
You left your pot with nothing in it, and the people's pot is hot and boiling. He means war.
His saying: ﴿We said: "Load into it two of each pair."﴾ That is, We said: "O Nuh, load into the ship of every pair, two, from among the animals on the earth, a male and a female."
Hafs read "min kullin" with tanwin on "kullin," meaning: from every thing, two pairs. The word "zawjan" (pair) applies to the two that cannot do without one another, and each of them is called a zawj, as one says of a man, "zawj," and of a woman, "zawj." The word "zawj" is also used for two when used as the opposite of the single, and it is used for a kind and a class. A similar usage is His saying: ﴿And it causes to grow from every pair a beautiful kind﴾ [al-Hajj: 5]. A similar usage is the saying of al-A'sha:
And every kind of brocade that Abu Hudhafah wears, he is concealed with it together.
He meant every class of brocade. ﴿And your family﴾ is conjoined to "zawjayn," or to "ithnayn" according to Hafs's reading, and it is in the accusative position of "kullin zawjayn," since it is the object of "ihmil." Or it is conjoined to "ithnayn" according to the reading of the majority. The intended meaning is: his wife, his sons, and their wives. ﴿Except those against whom the word has already preceded﴾, that is, those against whom the judgment has already been passed that they are among the drowned, in His saying: ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have done wrong; indeed they are to be drowned﴾, according to the earlier disagreement about them. So whoever considers them to be all the disbelievers, both of his family and others, makes this exception from the whole of "load into it two of each pair, two, and your family." Whoever says the intended ones are his son Kan'an and his wife Wa'ilah, mother of Kan'an, makes the exception from "your family." It will be a connected (muttasil) exception if "family" is understood in the broader sense, including believers and disbelievers among them, and a disconnected (munqati') exception if "family" means only the believers among them.
His saying: ﴿And those who believed﴾ is conjoined to "ahlaka," that is: and load into the ship those of your people who believed. He singled out the family for special care, or for the exception from them according to the other view.
Then Allah, glorified is He, described the fewness of the believers with Nuh in comparison with those who disbelieved in him, and said: ﴿And none believed with him except a few.﴾ It has been said they were eighty persons: among them three of his sons, Sam, Ham, and Yafith, and their wives. When they came out of the ship, they built a village called the village of the Eighty, which still exists in the region of Mosul. It has also been said they were ten, and it has been said seven, and it has been said they were seventy-two, and other things have been said.
His saying: ﴿And he said: "Embark therein."﴾ The speaker is Nuh, and it has been said it is Allah, glorified is He. The first is preferable, because of His saying: ﴿Indeed my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ Riding (rukub) is being upon the back of a thing, literally, as in "rakiba al-dabbah" (he rode the animal), or figuratively, as in "rakibahu al-dayn" (debt overwhelmed him). In the speech there is an ellipsis: that is, "embark, [and let the water run] in the ship," so it is not objected that "rakiba" transitive by itself. It has been said that the benefit of the added "fi" is that He commanded them to be inside the ship and not upon its back. It has also been said that it was added to indicate the place within the ship, as in His saying: ﴿And when they embarked in the ship﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 65], and His saying: ﴿Until, when they embarked in the ship﴾ [al-Kahf: 71]. It has been said: perhaps Nuh said this statement after loading what he had been commanded to carry of the pairs, as if it were said: so he carried the pairs and brought them into the ship, and he said to the believers. It is possible to say that he commanded all those commanded to be carried, of the pairs, the family, and the believers, to embark, and there is no impediment to the animals that do not understand understanding his address, or that this is according to the figure of speech of predominance (taghlib).
His saying: ﴿In the name of Allah﴾ is connected to "irkabu" (embark), or it is a circumstantial clause from its subject, that is: naming Allah, or saying: ﴿In the name of Allah is its course and its anchorage.﴾
The people of the two Sanctuaries (Makkah and Madinah) and the people of Basrah read "majraha" and "mursaha" with a damma on the mim in both, except those among them who deviated, as nouns of time, and they are in the accusative position as adverbs of time, that is: at the time of its running and its anchoring. They may also be verbal nouns, that is: at the time of its sailing and its mooring.
Al-A'mash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs read "majraha" with a fatha on the mim, and "mursaha" with a damma. Yahya ibn Wathhab read both with a fatha.
Mujahid, Sulayman ibn Jundub, 'Asim al-Jahdari, and Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi read "mujriha" and "mursiha" as attributes of Allah. They may also be in the nominative position by supposing an implied subject: that is, He is its runner and its anchorer. ﴿Indeed my Lord is Forgiving﴾ of sins, ﴿Merciful﴾ toward His servants. And of His mercy is the saving of this group, as a favor from Him, for the survival of this animal kind and so that it would not be uprooted by drowning.

This commentary is by al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 11, verses 35–44 (part 2 of 3):

﴿And it sailed with them amid waves like mountains.﴾ This clause is connected to an omitted clause that is indicated by the command to board. The implied sense is: so they boarded, saying the name of God, and it sailed with them. The word "mawj" (waves) is the plural of "mawja," which is what rises above the body of abundant water when the wind becomes strong. He compared the waves to mountains rising above the earth.

﴿And Noah called out to his son﴾. He is Kan'an. It was said that he was a disbeliever. It is considered unlikely that Noah would call out to someone who was a disbeliever, given his words: ﴿My Lord, leave not upon the earth from among the disbelievers a dweller.﴾ [Nuh: 26]. It is answered that he was a hypocrite, so Noah thought he was a believer. It was also said that the compassion of fatherhood moved him to this. It was also said that he was the son of his wife and not his son. This is supported by what is related: that Ali recited "and Noah called out to her son." It was also said that he was born out of wedlock and was born on Noah's bed.

It is refuted by the fact that the words ﴿And Noah called out to his son﴾ and his saying ﴿Indeed, my son is of my family﴾ refute that, along with its lack of preservation of the dignity of prophethood. ﴿And he was in isolation﴾, meaning in a place where he separated himself from his people and relatives, such that Noah's words "Board it" did not reach him. It was also said: in isolation from his father's religion. It was also said: away from the ship. It was said that this call was before people were certain of drowning, rather it was at the very first gushing forth of the oven (tannur).

﴿O my son, board with us.﴾

ʿĀṣim read it with a fatḥa on the yāʾ, and the rest read it with a kasra. As for the kasra, it is because he made it a substitute for the yāʾ of possession, since the original is "yā bunayya." As for the fatḥa, it is because the yāʾ of possession was changed into an alif for the lightness of the alif, then the alif was deleted and the fatḥa remained to indicate it.

Al-Naḥḥās said: The recitation of ʿĀṣim is problematic.

Abū Ḥātim said: Its origin is "yā bunayyāh," then it is deleted. Al-Zajjāj gave two possibilities for the fatḥa and two possibilities for the kasra.

As for the fatḥa, by the first possibility, it is what we have mentioned. The second possibility: the alif is deleted due to the meeting of two unvocalized letters (iltiqāʾ al-sākinayn).

As for the kasra, the first possibility is as we have mentioned, and the second is that it is deleted due to the meeting of two unvocalized letters. Thus al-Naḥḥās related it from him.

Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī and Ḥafṣ recited ﴿Board with us﴾ with the assimilation (idghām) of the bāʾ into the mīm, because the two are close in their point of articulation.

The rest recited without assimilation.

﴿And be not with the disbelievers﴾. He forbade him from being with the disbelievers, that is, outside the ship. It is possible that being with them is meant as being upon their religion.

Then God, glorified is He, related what Noah's son answered his father, so He said: ﴿He said, "I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water."﴾ That is, it will prevent the water from reaching me by its height. Noah answered him with his words: ﴿There is no protector today from the decree of God﴾, that is, there is no preventer, for it is a day upon which the punishment has become due and the pen has dried concerning what is to occur in it. He negated the genus of the protector, so the protector from drowning on that day is included under it in the first instance. He expressed the water, or the drowning, as "the decree of God" to magnify its matter and to make its affair terrifying.

As for the exception, al-Zajjāj said: it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), meaning: but whoever God has mercy upon, He protects him. So ﴿whom He has mercy upon﴾ is in the accusative position. It is permissible for the exception to be connected (muttaṣil), with "protector" meaning "one protected": that is, there is no one protected today from the decree of God except whom God has had mercy upon, like ﴿a gushing fluid﴾ [al-Ṭāriq: 6] and ﴿a pleasant life﴾ [al-Ḥāqqah: 21]. From this is the saying of the poet:

"Leave off nobility, do not rise to seek it,
and sit, for you are the one fed and clothed."

That is, the one fed and the one clothed. Ibn Jarīr chose this possibility. It was also said: "protector" means "one possessing protection," like "labin" and "tamir." The meaning is: there is no protector at all except in the place of whom God has had mercy upon, and that is the ship. In that case, there is no objection raised that says: the meaning of "whom He has had mercy upon" is "whom God has had mercy upon," and whom God has had mercy upon is protected, so how can his exception from the protector be valid? Because in each of these possibilities there is a removal of the problem.

It was also recited as "illā man rūḥima" (except whom He has had mercy upon) in the passive voice.

﴿And the wave came between them﴾, that is, it came between Noah and his son, so his escape from drowning became impossible. It was also said: between Noah's son and the mountain. The first is preferable, because the consequence ﴿so he was among the drowned﴾ that follows it indicates the first and not the second, since the mountain does not protect.

God said: ﴿And it was said, "O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold."﴾ It is said: "balaʿa al-māʾ yabluʿuhu" like "manaʿa yamnaʿu," and "baliʿa yableʿu" like "ḥamida yaḥmadu," two dialects related by al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ. And "al-balʿ" is drinking, and from it comes "al-bālūʿa," which is the place that drinks the water. And "al-izdirād" (swallowing). It is said: "balaʿa mā fī famihi min al-ṭaʿām" when he swallowed what was in his mouth of food. The verb "balʿ," which is an action of animals, was borrowed for absorption, indicating that this is not like the usual absorption that occurs gradually.

﴿And O sky, withhold.﴾ "Al-iqlāʿ" is withholding. It is said: "aqlaʿa al-maṭar" when the rain stopped.

The meaning is: He commanded the sky to withhold the water from being sent down. He placed the call to the earth before the sky because the beginning of the flood was from it.

﴿And the water subsided﴾, that is, decreased. It is said: "ghāḍa al-māʾ" and "ghuḍtuhu anā" (I caused it to subside).

﴿And the matter was decided﴾, that is, it was made firm and completed. He means: God destroyed the people of Noah in completeness and firmness.

﴿And it came to rest upon al-Jūdī﴾, that is, the ship settled upon the well-known mountain called al-Jūdī, which is a mountain near Mosul. It was also said: al-Jūdī is the name of every mountain. From this is the saying of Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl:

"Glory be to Him, then glory, we seek refuge in Him,
and before us, al-Jūdī and the rocks glorified Him."

It is said that it is from the mountains of Paradise, which is why the ship settled upon it.

﴿And it was said, "Away with the wrongdoing people."﴾ The speaker is God, glorified is He, to match the beginning of the verse. It was also said: it is Noah and his companions.

The meaning: and it was said, "Ruin for the wrongdoing people." This is one of the expressions specific to supplications of evil. He described them with wrongdoing to indicate that it is the cause of the destruction, and to allude to His saying: ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged﴾ [Hūd: 37].

The scholars of rhetoric have agreed that this noble verse reaches such a degree of eloquence and rhetoric that description falls short of it, and the capacity of those capable of the arts of rhetoric, firmly established in the science of eloquence, deeply rooted in the science of language, acquainted with what has been recorded from the sermons of the most eloquent orators of the Arabs and the poems of their most outstanding poets, and trained in the subtleties of the sciences and secrets of Arabic, is too weak to produce anything close to it.

A group of them has addressed the explanation of some of what it includes of this, and they were lengthy and excellent. May God have mercy upon us and them with His vast mercy.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Qatādah concerning His saying: ﴿then upon me is my crime﴾, he said: "my deed." ﴿And I am innocent of what you commit﴾, that is, of what you do.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from Qatādah concerning His saying: ﴿And it was revealed to Noah that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾, and that was when Noah invoked against them, and he said: ﴿My Lord, leave not upon the earth from among the disbelievers a dweller﴾ [Nuh: 26].

Aḥmad in al-Zuhd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abū al-Shaykh related from al-Ḥasan, who said: Noah did not invoke against his people until this verse was revealed, so his hope in them was cut off at that point, and he invoked against them.

Ibn Jarīr related from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying: ﴿So do not be distressed﴾, he said: "so do not grieve."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqī related from him concerning His saying: ﴿And construct the ship under Our eyes and Our revelation﴾, he said: "under God's eye and His revelation."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from him also, he said: Noah did not know how to build the ship, so God revealed to him to build it like the breast of a bird (jujuʾ al-ṭāʾir).

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh, al-Ḥākim and Ibn Mardawayh related from ʿĀʾishah, she said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Noah remained among his people for a thousand years less fifty years, calling them. Until, at the end of his time, he planted a tree, and it grew tall and spread in every direction. Then he cut it and began to shape it into a ship, and people would pass by and ask him, and he would say, 'I am making it into a ship.' They would mock him and say, 'He is making a ship on dry land! How will it sail?' He said, 'You will soon know.' When he finished it, and the oven gushed forth, and water increased in the lanes, the mother of the boy feared for him, for she loved him intensely. So she went out to the mountain until she reached a third of it. When the water reached her, she went up until she stood upon the mountain. When the water reached his neck, she lifted him before her until the water carried them off. Had God had mercy upon anyone among them, He would have had mercy upon the mother of the boy."

Al-Dhahabī criticized it in his addition to al-Ḥākim's Mustadrak.

Narrations and reports have been related concerning the description of the ship and its dimensions, but mentioning them here has little benefit.

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying: ﴿upon whom will come a punishment that disgraces him﴾, he said: "it is drowning." ﴿And there will descend upon him a lasting punishment﴾, he said: "it is abiding in the Fire."

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh and al-Ḥākim, who authenticated it, related from him: between the call of Noah and the destruction of his people there were three hundred years, and the oven gushed forth in India, and Noah's ship circled the House (of God) seven times.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim also related from him: "al-tannūr" is the spring in the island, the spring of al-Warda.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, who said: The oven gushed forth from the mosque of Kufa, from the direction of the gates of Kinda.

Similar to this has been related from him through several chains.

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: "al-tannūr" is the surface of the earth. It was said to him: when you see the water on the surface of the earth, board, you and those with you.

The Arabs call the surface of the earth "tannūr al-arḍ."

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir related from ʿAlī concerning ﴿and the oven gushed forth﴾, he said: "The dawn rose." It was said to him: when the dawn rises, board, you and your companions.

Other interpretations of "al-tannūr" have been related besides this, and we have already mentioned the reference to that.

Numerous narrations have been related concerning the description of the story, what Noah carried in the ship, how the drowning occurred, and how long the ship remained upon the surface of the water. [p. 660] They have no place in the explanation of the speech of God, glorified is He.

Ibn Jarīr related from Mujāhid concerning His saying: ﴿In the name of God is its course and its anchorage﴾, he said: "when they board, and when they set sail, and when they anchor."

Ibn Jarīr related from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, he said: When he wanted it to anchor, he said, "In the name of God," and it anchored; and when he wanted it to sail, he said, "In the name of God," and it sailed.

Abū Yaʿlā, al-Ṭabarānī, Ibn al-Sunnī, Ibn ʿAdī, Abū al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh related from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "A protection for my nation from drowning, when they board the ship, is that they say: 'In the name of God, the King, the Most Merciful, ﴿In the name of God is its course and its anchorage. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾' and ﴿They did not appraise God with the appraisal due to Him﴾ to the end of the verse."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim, al-Ṭabarānī and Ibn Mardawayh related it from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Abū al-Shaykh also related it from him as a marfūʿ report through another route.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Qatādah, he said: The name of Noah's son who drowned was Kanʿān.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: He was his son, except that he opposed him in intention and action.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from ʿIkrimah concerning His saying: ﴿There is no protector today from the decree of God except whom He has mercy upon﴾, he said: "No one is saved except the people of the ship."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from al-Qāsim ibn Abī Barra concerning His saying: ﴿And the wave came between them﴾, he said: "between Noah's son and the mountain."

Ibn al-Mundhir related from ʿIkrimah concerning His saying: ﴿O earth, swallow﴾, he said: "It is in Abyssinian (Ḥabashiyya)."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from Wahb ibn Munabbih concerning "iblaʿī," he said in Abyssinian: that is, "swallow it."

Abū al-Shaykh related from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, he said: Its meaning is "drink," in the language of India.

The Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 11, verses 35–44 (part 3 of 3):

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas the like of it.

I say: The occurrence of the word *al-bal'* (swallowing) and what is derived from it in the language of the Arabs is apparent and manifest, so what concern is it of ours with the Abyssinians and the Indians?

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 11, verses 35–44 (part 1 of 3):

.
His saying: ﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated it"?﴾ He, glorified is He, rebuked them for their saying that what was revealed to Nuh was a fabrication. He said: ﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated it"?﴾ Then He commanded him to respond with a fair statement, and said: ﴿Say: If I have fabricated it, upon me is my crime.﴾ With a kasra on the hamza, according to the recitation of the majority (qira'a, a recitational reading), it is a verbal noun from ajrama, meaning to commit what entails sin. Jarama and ajrama have the same meaning, as al-Nahhas said. The meaning is: upon me is my sin, or the recompense of my earning.
Whoever reads it with a fatha on the hamza says it is a plural. Al-Nahhas mentioned this. ﴿And I am innocent of what you commit (tajrimun)﴾, that is, innocent of your crime, because of what you attribute to me of fabrication. It has been said that there is an ellipsis in the speech, and the sense is: "But I have not fabricated it. So the crime and its punishment are only upon you, and I am innocent of it."
The exegetes differed concerning this verse. It has been said that it is a report about Nuh and what he said to his people. It has also been said that it is a report about the exchange that took place between our Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, and the disbelievers of Makkah.
The first view is preferable, because the speech before and after it is addressed to Nuh, peace be upon him.
His saying: ﴿And it was revealed to Nuh: "None of your people will believe except those who have already believed."﴾ The phrase "that he will not believe" is in the nominative position, as the deputy of the unnamed subject (na'ib al-fa'il).
It may also be in the accusative position, with the preposition bi- understood, meaning "that he..." The speech contains a discouragement for him regarding their faith: they persist in their disbelief, are determined upon it, and none of them will believe except those whose faith has already preceded. ﴿So do not grieve (tabta'is) over what they have been doing.﴾ Al-bu's means sorrow, that is, do not grieve. Al-ba'is means the one who is humbled. So Allah, glorified is He, forbade him from grieving the grief of one who is humbled, because ibti'as is grief accompanied by submission.
From this is the saying of the poet:
How many a friend or intimate have I lost, yet I did not grieve, though the loss in it is great.
Then, when Allah, glorified is He, informed him that they would never believe, He made him know the manner of their destruction, and inspired him with the matter by which he and those who believed with him would be saved. He said: ﴿And construct the ark under Our eyes and Our inspiration.﴾ That is: make the ship, while under Our eyes, that is, in Our sight. The intended meaning is Our protection and Our guarding of you. He expressed this by "eyes" because they are the instrument of sight, and sight is generally that by which protection and guarding occur. The plural "eyes" is used for magnification, not for multiplicity. It has been said that the meaning is "under Our eyes" meaning under the eyes of Our angels whom We made as eyes over your protection. It has been said: "under Our eyes" means with Our knowledge, and it has been said: by Our command.
The meaning of "by Our inspiration" is by what We revealed to you of the manner of its construction. ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have done wrong﴾, that is, do not request their respite, for the time of retribution against them has come. The clause ﴿indeed they are to be drowned﴾ is explanatory: that is, do not ask Us to delay them, for they are judged by Us to be drowned, and the decree has already passed, so there is no way to repel it or postpone it. It has been said: the meaning is, do not address Me about hastening their punishment, for they will be drowned at the appointed time for that, and their drowning will not be delayed beyond it. It has also been said: the intended "those who have done wrong" are his wife and his son.
﴿And he began constructing the ark﴾, that is, he began to make the ship, or he took up making the ship. It has been said that this is a report of a past state in order to bring the scene to mind. The clause ﴿and whenever a group of his people passed by him, they mocked him﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal), that is, they ridiculed him for building the ship.
Al-Akhfash and al-Kisa'i said: it is said "sakhira bihi" and "sakhira minhu."
Regarding the manner of their mockery of him, there are two views. The first is that they would see him building the ship and say: "O Nuh, after prophethood you have become a carpenter!" The second is that when they saw him building the ship, and they did not know it before that, they said: "O Nuh, what are you making?" He said: "I will sail it upon the water." So they marveled at his statement and mocked him.
Then he answered them with his saying: ﴿If you mock us, then we will mock you as you mock.﴾ This statement is resumptive, as if answering an implied question, as if it were said: "What did he say to them?" The meaning is: if you mock us today for our building of the ship, then we will mock you tomorrow at the time of drowning.
The meaning of mockery here is making them appear foolish: that is, if you make us look foolish, then we will make you look foolish as you do. His making them look foolish is with regard to his displaying it to them and addressing them directly; otherwise they were foolish before this and after it. The comparison in His saying ﴿as you mock﴾ is either for mere certainty and occurrence, or for renewal and repetition. The meaning is: we will mock you with a certain and actual mockery, just as you mock us, or with a renewed and repeated mockery, just as you mock us. It has also been said the meaning is: we will mock you in the future with a mockery like your mockery when the drowning overtakes you. There is a point to consider here, for their state at that time does not suit mockery, since they will be occupied by a preoccupying distress.
Then he threatened them with His saying: ﴿So you will come to know who will receive a punishment that disgraces him﴾. That is the punishment of drowning in this world. ﴿And there will descend upon him a lasting punishment﴾. That is the constant punishment of the Fire. The meaning of "yahill" (descends) is that it makes what was deferred immediate, derived from the falling due of a deferred debt. "Man" is a relative pronoun in the accusative position. It may also be interrogative in the nominative position, meaning: which of us will receive a punishment that disgraces him. It has also been said: it is in the nominative position as the inchoative, with "ya'tihi" as the predicate, and "yukhzihi" as an attribute of "adhab."
Al-Kisa'i said: some people of the Hijaz say "sawfa ta'lamun," and whoever says "sata'lamun" drops both the waw and the fa'. The Kufans permitted "sawfa ta'lamun," while the Basrans prohibited it. The intended "punishment of disgrace" is the punishment that disgraces its owner, and upon whom shame descends.
His saying: ﴿Until, when Our command came and the oven (tannur) boiled over﴾. "Hatta" here is the inceptive "hatta," which introduces a conditional clause, and it is made the end point (ghaya) of His saying: ﴿and construct the ark under Our eyes﴾.
The tannur has been interpreted in various ways. The first: it is the surface of the earth, and the Arabs call the surface of the earth a tannur. This is reported from Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, al-Zuhri, and Ibn 'Uyaynah.
The second: it is the oven in which they bake bread. This is the view of Mujahid, 'Ata' and al-Hasan, and it is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas.
The third: it is the place where water gathers in the ship. This is reported from al-Hasan.
The fourth: it is the break of dawn, from the expression "tannur al-fajr." This is reported from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib.
The fifth: it is the mosque of Kufah. This is reported from 'Ali as well and from Mujahid. Mujahid said: the tannur was on the side of Kufah.
The sixth: it is the high parts of the earth and the elevated places. This is said by Qatadah.
The seventh: it is the spring located in al-Jazirah called 'Ayn al-Wardah. This is reported from 'Ikrimah.
The eighth: it is a place in India. Ibn 'Abbas said: the tannur of Adam was in India.
Al-Nahhas said: these views are not contradictory, for Allah, glorified is He, has informed that the water came from the sky and the earth. He said: ﴿So We opened the gates of the sky with pouring water, and We caused the earth to burst forth with springs﴾ [al-Qamar 11–12]. So these views converge in that this was a sign. Thus he said. But there is a point to consider here, for the fourth view contradicts this convergence, and the interpretation by the gushing of water does not fit it, unless the intended meaning is merely the sign, as he mentioned at the end.
The lexicographers have mentioned that "fawr" means boiling, and that "tannur" is a foreign word which the Arabs arabicized. It has been said that the meaning of ﴿and the oven boiled over﴾ is an image of the arrival of the punishment, like the saying: "hamiya al-watis," meaning the battle became fierce. From this is the saying of the poet:
You left your pot with nothing in it, and the people's pot is hot and boiling. He means war.
His saying: ﴿We said: "Load into it two of each pair."﴾ That is, We said: "O Nuh, load into the ship of every pair, two, from among the animals on the earth, a male and a female."
Hafs read "min kullin" with tanwin on "kullin," meaning: from every thing, two pairs. The word "zawjan" (pair) applies to the two that cannot do without one another, and each of them is called a zawj, as one says of a man, "zawj," and of a woman, "zawj." The word "zawj" is also used for two when used as the opposite of the single, and it is used for a kind and a class. A similar usage is His saying: ﴿And it causes to grow from every pair a beautiful kind﴾ [al-Hajj: 5]. A similar usage is the saying of al-A'sha:
And every kind of brocade that Abu Hudhafah wears, he is concealed with it together.
He meant every class of brocade. ﴿And your family﴾ is conjoined to "zawjayn," or to "ithnayn" according to Hafs's reading, and it is in the accusative position of "kullin zawjayn," since it is the object of "ihmil." Or it is conjoined to "ithnayn" according to the reading of the majority. The intended meaning is: his wife, his sons, and their wives. ﴿Except those against whom the word has already preceded﴾, that is, those against whom the judgment has already been passed that they are among the drowned, in His saying: ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have done wrong; indeed they are to be drowned﴾, according to the earlier disagreement about them. So whoever considers them to be all the disbelievers, both of his family and others, makes this exception from the whole of "load into it two of each pair, two, and your family." Whoever says the intended ones are his son Kan'an and his wife Wa'ilah, mother of Kan'an, makes the exception from "your family." It will be a connected (muttasil) exception if "family" is understood in the broader sense, including believers and disbelievers among them, and a disconnected (munqati') exception if "family" means only the believers among them.
His saying: ﴿And those who believed﴾ is conjoined to "ahlaka," that is: and load into the ship those of your people who believed. He singled out the family for special care, or for the exception from them according to the other view.
Then Allah, glorified is He, described the fewness of the believers with Nuh in comparison with those who disbelieved in him, and said: ﴿And none believed with him except a few.﴾ It has been said they were eighty persons: among them three of his sons, Sam, Ham, and Yafith, and their wives. When they came out of the ship, they built a village called the village of the Eighty, which still exists in the region of Mosul. It has also been said they were ten, and it has been said seven, and it has been said they were seventy-two, and other things have been said.
His saying: ﴿And he said: "Embark therein."﴾ The speaker is Nuh, and it has been said it is Allah, glorified is He. The first is preferable, because of His saying: ﴿Indeed my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ Riding (rukub) is being upon the back of a thing, literally, as in "rakiba al-dabbah" (he rode the animal), or figuratively, as in "rakibahu al-dayn" (debt overwhelmed him). In the speech there is an ellipsis: that is, "embark, [and let the water run] in the ship," so it is not objected that "rakiba" transitive by itself. It has been said that the benefit of the added "fi" is that He commanded them to be inside the ship and not upon its back. It has also been said that it was added to indicate the place within the ship, as in His saying: ﴿And when they embarked in the ship﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 65], and His saying: ﴿Until, when they embarked in the ship﴾ [al-Kahf: 71]. It has been said: perhaps Nuh said this statement after loading what he had been commanded to carry of the pairs, as if it were said: so he carried the pairs and brought them into the ship, and he said to the believers. It is possible to say that he commanded all those commanded to be carried, of the pairs, the family, and the believers, to embark, and there is no impediment to the animals that do not understand understanding his address, or that this is according to the figure of speech of predominance (taghlib).
His saying: ﴿In the name of Allah﴾ is connected to "irkabu" (embark), or it is a circumstantial clause from its subject, that is: naming Allah, or saying: ﴿In the name of Allah is its course and its anchorage.﴾
The people of the two Sanctuaries (Makkah and Madinah) and the people of Basrah read "majraha" and "mursaha" with a damma on the mim in both, except those among them who deviated, as nouns of time, and they are in the accusative position as adverbs of time, that is: at the time of its running and its anchoring. They may also be verbal nouns, that is: at the time of its sailing and its mooring.
Al-A'mash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs read "majraha" with a fatha on the mim, and "mursaha" with a damma. Yahya ibn Wathhab read both with a fatha.
Mujahid, Sulayman ibn Jundub, 'Asim al-Jahdari, and Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi read "mujriha" and "mursiha" as attributes of Allah. They may also be in the nominative position by supposing an implied subject: that is, He is its runner and its anchorer. ﴿Indeed my Lord is Forgiving﴾ of sins, ﴿Merciful﴾ toward His servants. And of His mercy is the saving of this group, as a favor from Him, for the survival of this animal kind and so that it would not be uprooted by drowning.

This commentary is by al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 11, verses 35–44 (part 2 of 3):

﴿And it sailed with them amid waves like mountains.﴾ This clause is connected to an omitted clause that is indicated by the command to board. The implied sense is: so they boarded, saying the name of God, and it sailed with them. The word "mawj" (waves) is the plural of "mawja," which is what rises above the body of abundant water when the wind becomes strong. He compared the waves to mountains rising above the earth.

﴿And Noah called out to his son﴾. He is Kan'an. It was said that he was a disbeliever. It is considered unlikely that Noah would call out to someone who was a disbeliever, given his words: ﴿My Lord, leave not upon the earth from among the disbelievers a dweller.﴾ [Nuh: 26]. It is answered that he was a hypocrite, so Noah thought he was a believer. It was also said that the compassion of fatherhood moved him to this. It was also said that he was the son of his wife and not his son. This is supported by what is related: that Ali recited "and Noah called out to her son." It was also said that he was born out of wedlock and was born on Noah's bed.

It is refuted by the fact that the words ﴿And Noah called out to his son﴾ and his saying ﴿Indeed, my son is of my family﴾ refute that, along with its lack of preservation of the dignity of prophethood. ﴿And he was in isolation﴾, meaning in a place where he separated himself from his people and relatives, such that Noah's words "Board it" did not reach him. It was also said: in isolation from his father's religion. It was also said: away from the ship. It was said that this call was before people were certain of drowning, rather it was at the very first gushing forth of the oven (tannur).

﴿O my son, board with us.﴾

ʿĀṣim read it with a fatḥa on the yāʾ, and the rest read it with a kasra. As for the kasra, it is because he made it a substitute for the yāʾ of possession, since the original is "yā bunayya." As for the fatḥa, it is because the yāʾ of possession was changed into an alif for the lightness of the alif, then the alif was deleted and the fatḥa remained to indicate it.

Al-Naḥḥās said: The recitation of ʿĀṣim is problematic.

Abū Ḥātim said: Its origin is "yā bunayyāh," then it is deleted. Al-Zajjāj gave two possibilities for the fatḥa and two possibilities for the kasra.

As for the fatḥa, by the first possibility, it is what we have mentioned. The second possibility: the alif is deleted due to the meeting of two unvocalized letters (iltiqāʾ al-sākinayn).

As for the kasra, the first possibility is as we have mentioned, and the second is that it is deleted due to the meeting of two unvocalized letters. Thus al-Naḥḥās related it from him.

Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī and Ḥafṣ recited ﴿Board with us﴾ with the assimilation (idghām) of the bāʾ into the mīm, because the two are close in their point of articulation.

The rest recited without assimilation.

﴿And be not with the disbelievers﴾. He forbade him from being with the disbelievers, that is, outside the ship. It is possible that being with them is meant as being upon their religion.

Then God, glorified is He, related what Noah's son answered his father, so He said: ﴿He said, "I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water."﴾ That is, it will prevent the water from reaching me by its height. Noah answered him with his words: ﴿There is no protector today from the decree of God﴾, that is, there is no preventer, for it is a day upon which the punishment has become due and the pen has dried concerning what is to occur in it. He negated the genus of the protector, so the protector from drowning on that day is included under it in the first instance. He expressed the water, or the drowning, as "the decree of God" to magnify its matter and to make its affair terrifying.

As for the exception, al-Zajjāj said: it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), meaning: but whoever God has mercy upon, He protects him. So ﴿whom He has mercy upon﴾ is in the accusative position. It is permissible for the exception to be connected (muttaṣil), with "protector" meaning "one protected": that is, there is no one protected today from the decree of God except whom God has had mercy upon, like ﴿a gushing fluid﴾ [al-Ṭāriq: 6] and ﴿a pleasant life﴾ [al-Ḥāqqah: 21]. From this is the saying of the poet:

"Leave off nobility, do not rise to seek it,
and sit, for you are the one fed and clothed."

That is, the one fed and the one clothed. Ibn Jarīr chose this possibility. It was also said: "protector" means "one possessing protection," like "labin" and "tamir." The meaning is: there is no protector at all except in the place of whom God has had mercy upon, and that is the ship. In that case, there is no objection raised that says: the meaning of "whom He has had mercy upon" is "whom God has had mercy upon," and whom God has had mercy upon is protected, so how can his exception from the protector be valid? Because in each of these possibilities there is a removal of the problem.

It was also recited as "illā man rūḥima" (except whom He has had mercy upon) in the passive voice.

﴿And the wave came between them﴾, that is, it came between Noah and his son, so his escape from drowning became impossible. It was also said: between Noah's son and the mountain. The first is preferable, because the consequence ﴿so he was among the drowned﴾ that follows it indicates the first and not the second, since the mountain does not protect.

God said: ﴿And it was said, "O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold."﴾ It is said: "balaʿa al-māʾ yabluʿuhu" like "manaʿa yamnaʿu," and "baliʿa yableʿu" like "ḥamida yaḥmadu," two dialects related by al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ. And "al-balʿ" is drinking, and from it comes "al-bālūʿa," which is the place that drinks the water. And "al-izdirād" (swallowing). It is said: "balaʿa mā fī famihi min al-ṭaʿām" when he swallowed what was in his mouth of food. The verb "balʿ," which is an action of animals, was borrowed for absorption, indicating that this is not like the usual absorption that occurs gradually.

﴿And O sky, withhold.﴾ "Al-iqlāʿ" is withholding. It is said: "aqlaʿa al-maṭar" when the rain stopped.

The meaning is: He commanded the sky to withhold the water from being sent down. He placed the call to the earth before the sky because the beginning of the flood was from it.

﴿And the water subsided﴾, that is, decreased. It is said: "ghāḍa al-māʾ" and "ghuḍtuhu anā" (I caused it to subside).

﴿And the matter was decided﴾, that is, it was made firm and completed. He means: God destroyed the people of Noah in completeness and firmness.

﴿And it came to rest upon al-Jūdī﴾, that is, the ship settled upon the well-known mountain called al-Jūdī, which is a mountain near Mosul. It was also said: al-Jūdī is the name of every mountain. From this is the saying of Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl:

"Glory be to Him, then glory, we seek refuge in Him,
and before us, al-Jūdī and the rocks glorified Him."

It is said that it is from the mountains of Paradise, which is why the ship settled upon it.

﴿And it was said, "Away with the wrongdoing people."﴾ The speaker is God, glorified is He, to match the beginning of the verse. It was also said: it is Noah and his companions.

The meaning: and it was said, "Ruin for the wrongdoing people." This is one of the expressions specific to supplications of evil. He described them with wrongdoing to indicate that it is the cause of the destruction, and to allude to His saying: ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged﴾ [Hūd: 37].

The scholars of rhetoric have agreed that this noble verse reaches such a degree of eloquence and rhetoric that description falls short of it, and the capacity of those capable of the arts of rhetoric, firmly established in the science of eloquence, deeply rooted in the science of language, acquainted with what has been recorded from the sermons of the most eloquent orators of the Arabs and the poems of their most outstanding poets, and trained in the subtleties of the sciences and secrets of Arabic, is too weak to produce anything close to it.

A group of them has addressed the explanation of some of what it includes of this, and they were lengthy and excellent. May God have mercy upon us and them with His vast mercy.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Qatādah concerning His saying: ﴿then upon me is my crime﴾, he said: "my deed." ﴿And I am innocent of what you commit﴾, that is, of what you do.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from Qatādah concerning His saying: ﴿And it was revealed to Noah that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾, and that was when Noah invoked against them, and he said: ﴿My Lord, leave not upon the earth from among the disbelievers a dweller﴾ [Nuh: 26].

Aḥmad in al-Zuhd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abū al-Shaykh related from al-Ḥasan, who said: Noah did not invoke against his people until this verse was revealed, so his hope in them was cut off at that point, and he invoked against them.

Ibn Jarīr related from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying: ﴿So do not be distressed﴾, he said: "so do not grieve."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqī related from him concerning His saying: ﴿And construct the ship under Our eyes and Our revelation﴾, he said: "under God's eye and His revelation."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from him also, he said: Noah did not know how to build the ship, so God revealed to him to build it like the breast of a bird (jujuʾ al-ṭāʾir).

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh, al-Ḥākim and Ibn Mardawayh related from ʿĀʾishah, she said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Noah remained among his people for a thousand years less fifty years, calling them. Until, at the end of his time, he planted a tree, and it grew tall and spread in every direction. Then he cut it and began to shape it into a ship, and people would pass by and ask him, and he would say, 'I am making it into a ship.' They would mock him and say, 'He is making a ship on dry land! How will it sail?' He said, 'You will soon know.' When he finished it, and the oven gushed forth, and water increased in the lanes, the mother of the boy feared for him, for she loved him intensely. So she went out to the mountain until she reached a third of it. When the water reached her, she went up until she stood upon the mountain. When the water reached his neck, she lifted him before her until the water carried them off. Had God had mercy upon anyone among them, He would have had mercy upon the mother of the boy."

Al-Dhahabī criticized it in his addition to al-Ḥākim's Mustadrak.

Narrations and reports have been related concerning the description of the ship and its dimensions, but mentioning them here has little benefit.

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying: ﴿upon whom will come a punishment that disgraces him﴾, he said: "it is drowning." ﴿And there will descend upon him a lasting punishment﴾, he said: "it is abiding in the Fire."

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh and al-Ḥākim, who authenticated it, related from him: between the call of Noah and the destruction of his people there were three hundred years, and the oven gushed forth in India, and Noah's ship circled the House (of God) seven times.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim also related from him: "al-tannūr" is the spring in the island, the spring of al-Warda.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, who said: The oven gushed forth from the mosque of Kufa, from the direction of the gates of Kinda.

Similar to this has been related from him through several chains.

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: "al-tannūr" is the surface of the earth. It was said to him: when you see the water on the surface of the earth, board, you and those with you.

The Arabs call the surface of the earth "tannūr al-arḍ."

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir related from ʿAlī concerning ﴿and the oven gushed forth﴾, he said: "The dawn rose." It was said to him: when the dawn rises, board, you and your companions.

Other interpretations of "al-tannūr" have been related besides this, and we have already mentioned the reference to that.

Numerous narrations have been related concerning the description of the story, what Noah carried in the ship, how the drowning occurred, and how long the ship remained upon the surface of the water. [p. 660] They have no place in the explanation of the speech of God, glorified is He.

Ibn Jarīr related from Mujāhid concerning His saying: ﴿In the name of God is its course and its anchorage﴾, he said: "when they board, and when they set sail, and when they anchor."

Ibn Jarīr related from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, he said: When he wanted it to anchor, he said, "In the name of God," and it anchored; and when he wanted it to sail, he said, "In the name of God," and it sailed.

Abū Yaʿlā, al-Ṭabarānī, Ibn al-Sunnī, Ibn ʿAdī, Abū al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh related from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "A protection for my nation from drowning, when they board the ship, is that they say: 'In the name of God, the King, the Most Merciful, ﴿In the name of God is its course and its anchorage. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾' and ﴿They did not appraise God with the appraisal due to Him﴾ to the end of the verse."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim, al-Ṭabarānī and Ibn Mardawayh related it from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Abū al-Shaykh also related it from him as a marfūʿ report through another route.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Qatādah, he said: The name of Noah's son who drowned was Kanʿān.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: He was his son, except that he opposed him in intention and action.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from ʿIkrimah concerning His saying: ﴿There is no protector today from the decree of God except whom He has mercy upon﴾, he said: "No one is saved except the people of the ship."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from al-Qāsim ibn Abī Barra concerning His saying: ﴿And the wave came between them﴾, he said: "between Noah's son and the mountain."

Ibn al-Mundhir related from ʿIkrimah concerning His saying: ﴿O earth, swallow﴾, he said: "It is in Abyssinian (Ḥabashiyya)."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from Wahb ibn Munabbih concerning "iblaʿī," he said in Abyssinian: that is, "swallow it."

Abū al-Shaykh related from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, he said: Its meaning is "drink," in the language of India.

The Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 11, verses 35–44 (part 3 of 3):

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas the like of it.

I say: The occurrence of the word *al-bal'* (swallowing) and what is derived from it in the language of the Arabs is apparent and manifest, so what concern is it of ours with the Abyssinians and the Indians?

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 11, verses 35–44 (part 1 of 3):

.
His saying: ﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated it"?﴾ He, glorified is He, rebuked them for their saying that what was revealed to Nuh was a fabrication. He said: ﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated it"?﴾ Then He commanded him to respond with a fair statement, and said: ﴿Say: If I have fabricated it, upon me is my crime.﴾ With a kasra on the hamza, according to the recitation of the majority (qira'a, a recitational reading), it is a verbal noun from ajrama, meaning to commit what entails sin. Jarama and ajrama have the same meaning, as al-Nahhas said. The meaning is: upon me is my sin, or the recompense of my earning.
Whoever reads it with a fatha on the hamza says it is a plural. Al-Nahhas mentioned this. ﴿And I am innocent of what you commit (tajrimun)﴾, that is, innocent of your crime, because of what you attribute to me of fabrication. It has been said that there is an ellipsis in the speech, and the sense is: "But I have not fabricated it. So the crime and its punishment are only upon you, and I am innocent of it."
The exegetes differed concerning this verse. It has been said that it is a report about Nuh and what he said to his people. It has also been said that it is a report about the exchange that took place between our Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, and the disbelievers of Makkah.
The first view is preferable, because the speech before and after it is addressed to Nuh, peace be upon him.
His saying: ﴿And it was revealed to Nuh: "None of your people will believe except those who have already believed."﴾ The phrase "that he will not believe" is in the nominative position, as the deputy of the unnamed subject (na'ib al-fa'il).
It may also be in the accusative position, with the preposition bi- understood, meaning "that he..." The speech contains a discouragement for him regarding their faith: they persist in their disbelief, are determined upon it, and none of them will believe except those whose faith has already preceded. ﴿So do not grieve (tabta'is) over what they have been doing.﴾ Al-bu's means sorrow, that is, do not grieve. Al-ba'is means the one who is humbled. So Allah, glorified is He, forbade him from grieving the grief of one who is humbled, because ibti'as is grief accompanied by submission.
From this is the saying of the poet:
How many a friend or intimate have I lost, yet I did not grieve, though the loss in it is great.
Then, when Allah, glorified is He, informed him that they would never believe, He made him know the manner of their destruction, and inspired him with the matter by which he and those who believed with him would be saved. He said: ﴿And construct the ark under Our eyes and Our inspiration.﴾ That is: make the ship, while under Our eyes, that is, in Our sight. The intended meaning is Our protection and Our guarding of you. He expressed this by "eyes" because they are the instrument of sight, and sight is generally that by which protection and guarding occur. The plural "eyes" is used for magnification, not for multiplicity. It has been said that the meaning is "under Our eyes" meaning under the eyes of Our angels whom We made as eyes over your protection. It has been said: "under Our eyes" means with Our knowledge, and it has been said: by Our command.
The meaning of "by Our inspiration" is by what We revealed to you of the manner of its construction. ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have done wrong﴾, that is, do not request their respite, for the time of retribution against them has come. The clause ﴿indeed they are to be drowned﴾ is explanatory: that is, do not ask Us to delay them, for they are judged by Us to be drowned, and the decree has already passed, so there is no way to repel it or postpone it. It has been said: the meaning is, do not address Me about hastening their punishment, for they will be drowned at the appointed time for that, and their drowning will not be delayed beyond it. It has also been said: the intended "those who have done wrong" are his wife and his son.
﴿And he began constructing the ark﴾, that is, he began to make the ship, or he took up making the ship. It has been said that this is a report of a past state in order to bring the scene to mind. The clause ﴿and whenever a group of his people passed by him, they mocked him﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal), that is, they ridiculed him for building the ship.
Al-Akhfash and al-Kisa'i said: it is said "sakhira bihi" and "sakhira minhu."
Regarding the manner of their mockery of him, there are two views. The first is that they would see him building the ship and say: "O Nuh, after prophethood you have become a carpenter!" The second is that when they saw him building the ship, and they did not know it before that, they said: "O Nuh, what are you making?" He said: "I will sail it upon the water." So they marveled at his statement and mocked him.
Then he answered them with his saying: ﴿If you mock us, then we will mock you as you mock.﴾ This statement is resumptive, as if answering an implied question, as if it were said: "What did he say to them?" The meaning is: if you mock us today for our building of the ship, then we will mock you tomorrow at the time of drowning.
The meaning of mockery here is making them appear foolish: that is, if you make us look foolish, then we will make you look foolish as you do. His making them look foolish is with regard to his displaying it to them and addressing them directly; otherwise they were foolish before this and after it. The comparison in His saying ﴿as you mock﴾ is either for mere certainty and occurrence, or for renewal and repetition. The meaning is: we will mock you with a certain and actual mockery, just as you mock us, or with a renewed and repeated mockery, just as you mock us. It has also been said the meaning is: we will mock you in the future with a mockery like your mockery when the drowning overtakes you. There is a point to consider here, for their state at that time does not suit mockery, since they will be occupied by a preoccupying distress.
Then he threatened them with His saying: ﴿So you will come to know who will receive a punishment that disgraces him﴾. That is the punishment of drowning in this world. ﴿And there will descend upon him a lasting punishment﴾. That is the constant punishment of the Fire. The meaning of "yahill" (descends) is that it makes what was deferred immediate, derived from the falling due of a deferred debt. "Man" is a relative pronoun in the accusative position. It may also be interrogative in the nominative position, meaning: which of us will receive a punishment that disgraces him. It has also been said: it is in the nominative position as the inchoative, with "ya'tihi" as the predicate, and "yukhzihi" as an attribute of "adhab."
Al-Kisa'i said: some people of the Hijaz say "sawfa ta'lamun," and whoever says "sata'lamun" drops both the waw and the fa'. The Kufans permitted "sawfa ta'lamun," while the Basrans prohibited it. The intended "punishment of disgrace" is the punishment that disgraces its owner, and upon whom shame descends.
