Abū Ḥātim said: Its origin is "yā bunayyāh," then it is deleted. Al-Zajjāj gave two possibilities for the fatḥa and two possibilities for the kasra.

As for the fatḥa, by the first possibility, it is what we have mentioned. The second possibility: the alif is deleted due to the meeting of two unvocalized letters (iltiqāʾ al-sākinayn).

As for the kasra, the first possibility is as we have mentioned, and the second is that it is deleted due to the meeting of two unvocalized letters. Thus al-Naḥḥās related it from him.

Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī and Ḥafṣ recited ﴿Board with us﴾ with the assimilation (idghām) of the bāʾ into the mīm, because the two are close in their point of articulation.

The rest recited without assimilation.

﴿And be not with the disbelievers﴾. He forbade him from being with the disbelievers, that is, outside the ship. It is possible that being with them is meant as being upon their religion.

Then God, glorified is He, related what Noah's son answered his father, so He said: ﴿He said, "I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water."﴾ That is, it will prevent the water from reaching me by its height. Noah answered him with his words: ﴿There is no protector today from the decree of God﴾, that is, there is no preventer, for it is a day upon which the punishment has become due and the pen has dried concerning what is to occur in it. He negated the genus of the protector, so the protector from drowning on that day is included under it in the first instance. He expressed the water, or the drowning, as "the decree of God" to magnify its matter and to make its affair terrifying.

As for the exception, al-Zajjāj said: it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), meaning: but whoever God has mercy upon, He protects him. So ﴿whom He has mercy upon﴾ is in the accusative position. It is permissible for the exception to be connected (muttaṣil), with "protector" meaning "one protected": that is, there is no one protected today from the decree of God except whom God has had mercy upon, like ﴿a gushing fluid﴾ [al-Ṭāriq: 6] and ﴿a pleasant life﴾ [al-Ḥāqqah: 21]. From this is the saying of the poet:

"Leave off nobility, do not rise to seek it,
and sit, for you are the one fed and clothed."

That is, the one fed and the one clothed. Ibn Jarīr chose this possibility. It was also said: "protector" means "one possessing protection," like "labin" and "tamir." The meaning is: there is no protector at all except in the place of whom God has had mercy upon, and that is the ship. In that case, there is no objection raised that says: the meaning of "whom He has had mercy upon" is "whom God has had mercy upon," and whom God has had mercy upon is protected, so how can his exception from the protector be valid? Because in each of these possibilities there is a removal of the problem.

It was also recited as "illā man rūḥima" (except whom He has had mercy upon) in the passive voice.

﴿And the wave came between them﴾, that is, it came between Noah and his son, so his escape from drowning became impossible. It was also said: between Noah's son and the mountain. The first is preferable, because the consequence ﴿so he was among the drowned﴾ that follows it indicates the first and not the second, since the mountain does not protect.

God said: ﴿And it was said, "O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold."﴾ It is said: "balaʿa al-māʾ yabluʿuhu" like "manaʿa yamnaʿu," and "baliʿa yableʿu" like "ḥamida yaḥmadu," two dialects related by al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ. And "al-balʿ" is drinking, and from it comes "al-bālūʿa," which is the place that drinks the water. And "al-izdirād" (swallowing). It is said: "balaʿa mā fī famihi min al-ṭaʿām" when he swallowed what was in his mouth of food. The verb "balʿ," which is an action of animals, was borrowed for absorption, indicating that this is not like the usual absorption that occurs gradually.

﴿And O sky, withhold.﴾ "Al-iqlāʿ" is withholding. It is said: "aqlaʿa al-maṭar" when the rain stopped.

The meaning is: He commanded the sky to withhold the water from being sent down. He placed the call to the earth before the sky because the beginning of the flood was from it.

﴿And the water subsided﴾, that is, decreased. It is said: "ghāḍa al-māʾ" and "ghuḍtuhu anā" (I caused it to subside).

﴿And the matter was decided﴾, that is, it was made firm and completed. He means: God destroyed the people of Noah in completeness and firmness.

﴿And it came to rest upon al-Jūdī﴾, that is, the ship settled upon the well-known mountain called al-Jūdī, which is a mountain near Mosul. It was also said: al-Jūdī is the name of every mountain. From this is the saying of Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl:

"Glory be to Him, then glory, we seek refuge in Him,
and before us, al-Jūdī and the rocks glorified Him."

It is said that it is from the mountains of Paradise, which is why the ship settled upon it.

﴿And it was said, "Away with the wrongdoing people."﴾ The speaker is God, glorified is He, to match the beginning of the verse. It was also said: it is Noah and his companions.

The meaning: and it was said, "Ruin for the wrongdoing people." This is one of the expressions specific to supplications of evil. He described them with wrongdoing to indicate that it is the cause of the destruction, and to allude to His saying: ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged﴾ [Hūd: 37].

The scholars of rhetoric have agreed that this noble verse reaches such a degree of eloquence and rhetoric that description falls short of it, and the capacity of those capable of the arts of rhetoric, firmly established in the science of eloquence, deeply rooted in the science of language, acquainted with what has been recorded from the sermons of the most eloquent orators of the Arabs and the poems of their most outstanding poets, and trained in the subtleties of the sciences and secrets of Arabic, is too weak to produce anything close to it.

A group of them has addressed the explanation of some of what it includes of this, and they were lengthy and excellent. May God have mercy upon us and them with His vast mercy.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Qatādah concerning His saying: ﴿then upon me is my crime﴾, he said: "my deed." ﴿And I am innocent of what you commit﴾, that is, of what you do.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from Qatādah concerning His saying: ﴿And it was revealed to Noah that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾, and that was when Noah invoked against them, and he said: ﴿My Lord, leave not upon the earth from among the disbelievers a dweller﴾ [Nuh: 26].

Aḥmad in al-Zuhd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abū al-Shaykh related from al-Ḥasan, who said: Noah did not invoke against his people until this verse was revealed, so his hope in them was cut off at that point, and he invoked against them.

Ibn Jarīr related from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying: ﴿So do not be distressed﴾, he said: "so do not grieve."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqī related from him concerning His saying: ﴿And construct the ship under Our eyes and Our revelation﴾, he said: "under God's eye and His revelation."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from him also, he said: Noah did not know how to build the ship, so God revealed to him to build it like the breast of a bird (jujuʾ al-ṭāʾir).

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh, al-Ḥākim and Ibn Mardawayh related from ʿĀʾishah, she said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Noah remained among his people for a thousand years less fifty years, calling them. Until, at the end of his time, he planted a tree, and it grew tall and spread in every direction. Then he cut it and began to shape it into a ship, and people would pass by and ask him, and he would say, 'I am making it into a ship.' They would mock him and say, 'He is making a ship on dry land! How will it sail?' He said, 'You will soon know.' When he finished it, and the oven gushed forth, and water increased in the lanes, the mother of the boy feared for him, for she loved him intensely. So she went out to the mountain until she reached a third of it. When the water reached her, she went up until she stood upon the mountain. When the water reached his neck, she lifted him before her until the water carried them off. Had God had mercy upon anyone among them, He would have had mercy upon the mother of the boy."

Al-Dhahabī criticized it in his addition to al-Ḥākim's Mustadrak.

Narrations and reports have been related concerning the description of the ship and its dimensions, but mentioning them here has little benefit.

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying: ﴿upon whom will come a punishment that disgraces him﴾, he said: "it is drowning." ﴿And there will descend upon him a lasting punishment﴾, he said: "it is abiding in the Fire."

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh and al-Ḥākim, who authenticated it, related from him: between the call of Noah and the destruction of his people there were three hundred years, and the oven gushed forth in India, and Noah's ship circled the House (of God) seven times.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim also related from him: "al-tannūr" is the spring in the island, the spring of al-Warda.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, who said: The oven gushed forth from the mosque of Kufa, from the direction of the gates of Kinda.

Similar to this has been related from him through several chains.

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: "al-tannūr" is the surface of the earth. It was said to him: when you see the water on the surface of the earth, board, you and those with you.

The Arabs call the surface of the earth "tannūr al-arḍ."

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir related from ʿAlī concerning ﴿and the oven gushed forth﴾, he said: "The dawn rose." It was said to him: when the dawn rises, board, you and your companions.

Other interpretations of "al-tannūr" have been related besides this, and we have already mentioned the reference to that.

Numerous narrations have been related concerning the description of the story, what Noah carried in the ship, how the drowning occurred, and how long the ship remained upon the surface of the water. [p. 660] They have no place in the explanation of the speech of God, glorified is He.

Ibn Jarīr related from Mujāhid concerning His saying: ﴿In the name of God is its course and its anchorage﴾, he said: "when they board, and when they set sail, and when they anchor."

Ibn Jarīr related from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, he said: When he wanted it to anchor, he said, "In the name of God," and it anchored; and when he wanted it to sail, he said, "In the name of God," and it sailed.

Abū Yaʿlā, al-Ṭabarānī, Ibn al-Sunnī, Ibn ʿAdī, Abū al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh related from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "A protection for my nation from drowning, when they board the ship, is that they say: 'In the name of God, the King, the Most Merciful, ﴿In the name of God is its course and its anchorage. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾' and ﴿They did not appraise God with the appraisal due to Him﴾ to the end of the verse."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim, al-Ṭabarānī and Ibn Mardawayh related it from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Abū al-Shaykh also related it from him as a marfūʿ report through another route.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Qatādah, he said: The name of Noah's son who drowned was Kanʿān.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: He was his son, except that he opposed him in intention and action.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from ʿIkrimah concerning His saying: ﴿There is no protector today from the decree of God except whom He has mercy upon﴾, he said: "No one is saved except the people of the ship."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from al-Qāsim ibn Abī Barra concerning His saying: ﴿And the wave came between them﴾, he said: "between Noah's son and the mountain."

Ibn al-Mundhir related from ʿIkrimah concerning His saying: ﴿O earth, swallow﴾, he said: "It is in Abyssinian (Ḥabashiyya)."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh related from Wahb ibn Munabbih concerning "iblaʿī," he said in Abyssinian: that is, "swallow it."

Abū al-Shaykh related from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, he said: Its meaning is "drink," in the language of India.

The Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 11, verses 35–44 (part 3 of 3):

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas the like of it.

I say: The occurrence of the word *al-bal'* (swallowing) and what is derived from it in the language of the Arabs is apparent and manifest, so what concern is it of ours with the Abyssinians and the Indians?

The commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 11, verses 45–49:

.

The meaning of ﴿And Noah called out to his Lord﴾ is that he called upon Him. What is intended is that he intended to supplicate, as shown by the fa' (so/then) in ﴿so he said, "My Lord, indeed my son is of my family"﴾. Conjoining a thing with itself is not permissible, so the aforementioned supposition (taqdir) is necessary. The commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 11, verses 45–49:

.

The meaning of ﴿And Noah called out to his Lord﴾ is that he called upon Him. What is intended is that he intended to supplicate, as shown by the fa' (so/then) in ﴿so he said, "My Lord, indeed my son is of my family"﴾. Conjoining a thing with itself is not permissible, so the aforementioned supposition (taqdir) is necessary. The meaning of his words ﴿indeed my son is of my family﴾ is that he is among the family whom You promised to save when You said, "and your family."

If it is asked: how could Noah, peace be upon him, request the fulfilment of what God promised him with His words "and your family," while the exception that restricts it, ﴿except those against whom the word has already preceded﴾, was left out? It is answered: he did not know at that time that he was among those against whom the word had preceded, for he thought him to be among the believers. ﴿And indeed Your promise is the truth﴾, which admits no failure. And this is from him: ﴿and You are the most just of judges﴾, meaning the most perfect of those who perfect what judgment entails, so that no annulment can reach Your judgment. It has been said that he meant by "the most just of judges" the most knowledgeable of them and the most equitable: that is, You are more knowledgeable and more just than those who hold judgment. It has also been said that al-Hakim (the judge) here means dhu al-hikmah (the possessor of wisdom), as in dari' (armoured one).

Then God, glorified is He, answered Noah by making clear that his son was not included in the general sense of "family," and that he was excluded by the qualification of the exception, in His words: ﴿He said, "O Noah, indeed he is not of your family"﴾, those who believed in you and followed you, even though he was of your family by kinship. Then He stated explicitly the cause that necessitates his exclusion from the general sense of "family," clarifying that what is meant by kinship is kinship of religion, not kinship of lineage alone, so He said: ﴿Indeed, he is one whose deeds are not righteous﴾.

Ibn al-Arabi said: this is an addition from God and an admonition by which He raises Noah above the station of the ignorant and elevates him by it to the station of the scholars who act.

Then, when Noah knew that his request did not correspond to reality, and that his supplication arose from a delusion he had imagined, he hastened to acknowledge the error and to seek forgiveness and mercy. So he ﴿said, "My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You about that of which I have no knowledge"﴾, meaning: I seek refuge in You from asking of You what I have no knowledge of as to its soundness and permissibility. ﴿And unless You forgive me﴾ the sin of what I supplicated for without knowledge from myself, ﴿and have mercy upon me﴾ with Your mercy which encompasses all things, so that You accept my repentance, ﴿I would be among the losers﴾ in my deeds, so that I gain nothing from them.

The speaker is God, or the angels: ﴿It was said, "O Noah, descend"﴾, that is, come down from the ship to the earth, or from the mountain to the lower part of the earth, for the earth had swallowed its water and dried up. ﴿With peace from Us﴾, that is, with safety and security. It has been said: with greeting and blessings, that is, lasting bounties, derived from the kneeling of the camel (burrukh al-jamal), which means its settling, and from it comes barakah (blessing), for water settles in it. In this address to him there is evidence of the acceptance of his repentance and the forgiveness of his slip. ﴿And upon nations among those with you﴾ (p-661), that is, nations arising from those with you, and they are those who branched out from the offspring of whoever was with him in the ship. It has been said: what is meant is those in the ship, for they were diverse nations and varied kinds of animals.

It has been said: by these nations who were with him, God, glorified is He, meant whoever among their offspring became a believer, and by His words ﴿and nations We will provide for, then there will touch them from Us a painful punishment﴾ He meant whoever among their offspring became a disbeliever until the Day of Resurrection. **Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 11, verses 50–60:**

His saying, ﴿And to ʿĀd, their brother Hūd﴾, is coordinated with "And We sent Nūḥ" (*maʿṭūf ʿalā*). That is: and We sent to ʿĀd their brother, meaning one of them. Hūd is an explanatory apposition (*ʿaṭf bayān*, appositive clarification). The people of ʿĀd were worshippers of idols, and something similar has already been discussed in al-Aʿrāf.

It has been said: they are the First ʿĀd and the Last ʿĀd. The First ʿĀd and the Last ʿĀd are Shaddād and Luqmān and their people, who are mentioned in His saying, ﴿Iram of the lofty pillars﴾ [al-Fajr: 7]. The origin of "ʿĀd" is the name of a man, and then it became the name of a tribe, like Tamīm and Bakr and similar names.

﴿You have no god other than Him﴾: it is read *ghayruhu* with a kasra on the basis of the wording, and with a damma on the basis of the position of *min ilāhin* (the place of the word after the preposition), and it is read with a fatḥa as an exception (*istithnāʾ*). ﴿You are nothing but fabricators﴾: that is, you are not, in taking a god other than Allah, anything but liars against Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Then he addressed them, saying: ﴿O my people, I do not ask you for any reward for it﴾: that is, I do not seek from you any reward for what I convey to you and advise you about, of guidance to the worship of Allah alone and that you have no god besides Him. So the pronoun refers to the content of this speech.

The meaning of this has already been mentioned in the story of Nūḥ: ﴿My reward is only from the One who originated me﴾, that is, my reward that I seek is only from the One who originated me, meaning created me; He is the One who will reward me for that. ﴿Will you not reason?﴾ that the reward of those who give sincere advice is only from the Lord of the worlds. It has been said: in what preceded, in the story of Nūḥ, he said *mālan* (wealth), but here he said *ajran* (reward), because of the mention of the treasuries after it in the story of Nūḥ, and the word "wealth" is more fitting there.

Then he guided them to seeking forgiveness and repentance.

The meaning is: seek His forgiveness for what has passed of your sins, then draw near to Him through repentance.

A fuller explanation of something similar has already been given in the story of Nūḥ. Then he encouraged them to believe with the promise of immediate good, saying: ﴿He will send the sky﴾, that is, the rain, ﴿upon you in abundance﴾, that is, abundant in its pouring. It is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (*ḥāl*). The sky poured, pours, and so it is abundant (*midrār*). The people of Hūd were people of gardens, crops, and prosperity, and their dwellings were the sands that lay between al-Shām and al-Yaman. ﴿And He will add strength to your strength﴾ is coordinated with "He will send": that is, added might to your might, or fertility to your fertility, or honor to your honor.

al-Zajjāj said: the meaning is "He will add to you strength in blessings."

﴿And do not turn away as criminals﴾: that is, do not turn away from what I call you to and persist in disbelief, insisting upon it. *Ijrām* (criminality) means sins, as has already been mentioned.

Then his people answered him with what indicates their extreme ignorance and great stupidity: ﴿They said, "O Hūd, you have not brought us any clear proof"﴾, that is, any evident argument that we could act upon and believe you on account of it, while not acknowledging the proofs and demonstrations of Allah that had come to them, out of obstinacy and distance from the truth. ﴿And we will not abandon our gods﴾ which we worship besides Allah.

The meaning of ﴿on your word﴾ is "departing from your word," so the adverbial phrase is in the accusative place as a circumstantial state. ﴿And we are not believers in you﴾: that is, we will not believe you regarding anything of what you have brought.

﴿We only say that some of our gods have struck you with some evil﴾: that is, we say only that some of our gods, which you disparage and which you deem foolish in our worship, have afflicted you with evil, namely madness, so that what you say to us and repeat to us of warning against them has arisen from your madness. It is said: *ʿarāhu al-amr* and *iʿtarāhu* means when a matter befalls him.

So he answered them with what indicates his indifference to them, his confidence in his Lord, and his reliance upon Him, and that they have no power over anything that the disbelievers want to do to him; rather, Allah, glorified is He, is the One who harms and benefits. So ﴿He said, "I call Allah to witness, and you bear witness"﴾ that ﴿I am free from what you associate﴾ with Him.

﴿Besides Him﴾: that is, from your associating others with Allah besides Allah, without Allah having sent down any authority for it. ﴿So scheme against me, all of you﴾: you and your gods, if they are as you claim, able to harm me and that they have afflicted me with evil. ﴿Then do not give me respite﴾: that is, do not delay me, but hasten against me and do what you will. In this there is a display of indifference to them and to their idols, which they worship, that would strike their ears, and it makes clear their helplessness and their inability over anything.

﴿Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord﴾: so He will protect me from your scheming, and even if you reach every extent in seeking ways to harm me, whoever relies upon Allah, He suffices him.

Then, when he had shown them his reliance upon Allah and his confidence in His protection and guardianship, he described Him with what necessitates reliance upon Him and entrusting oneself to Him: that His lordship encompasses Him and them, and that He is the owner of all things, and that the forelock of every creature among the creatures of the earth is in His hand, in His grip and under His subjugation. This is an image of the utmost subjugation and the ultimate humbling. When they took a captive and wanted to release him and bestow favor upon him, they would cut his forelock, making that a sign of his subjugation.

al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning of *ākhidhun bi-nāṣiyatihā* (one who takes hold of its forelock) is its owner and the one who has power over it. al-Qutaybī said: its subduer, because whoever you take by the forelock, you have subdued him. The *nāṣiyah* is the hair at the front of the head.

Then he gave the reason for what preceded with his saying: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is upon a straight path﴾: that is, He is upon truth and justice, so He hardly lets you dominate me.

﴿But if you turn away﴾: that is, you are persisting in turning away, so one of the two *tāʾs* was dropped. The meaning: if you persist in turning away from responding and insist upon what you are on of disbelief, ﴿then I have already conveyed to you what I was sent with to you﴾. There is nothing upon me but that, and the proof has already been established against you. ﴿And my Lord will replace you with another people﴾: this is a new sentence affirming the threat of destruction, that is: He will install in your dwellings and your wealth other people. It is also possible that it is coordinated with ﴿I have already conveyed to you﴾.

Ḥafṣ narrated from ʿĀṣim that he recited *wa-yastakhlif* with a jazm (apocopation), taking it as modifying the position of ﴿I have already conveyed to you﴾. ﴿And you will not harm Him at all﴾: that is, by your turning away, and you will not be able to cause much harm or little. ﴿Indeed, my Lord is over all things a guardian﴾: that is, a watchful overseer over it who protects it from everything. It has been said: *ʿalā* here has the meaning of *li-* (for), so the meaning is "a guardian for everything," and so He protects me from your reaching me with any evil.

﴿And when Our command came﴾: that is, Our punishment, which is the destruction of ʿĀd, ﴿We saved Hūd and those who believed with him﴾ from among his people, ﴿by a mercy from Us﴾: that is, by a great mercy from Us, because no one is saved except by the mercy of Allah. It has been said that it is faith. ﴿From a harsh punishment﴾: that is, severe. It has been said that it was the *samūm* (scorching wind) which used to enter their noses.

﴿And those were ʿĀd﴾ is a subject and predicate, and the demonstrative was feminine in consideration of the tribe.

al-Kisāʾī said: among the Arabs are those who do not give *ʿĀd* the diptote-declension (*ṣarf*), and make it the name of the tribe. ﴿They denied the signs of their Lord﴾: that is, they disbelieved in them, denied them, and rejected the miracles. ﴿And they disobeyed His messengers﴾: that is, Hūd alone, because there was no other messenger in his time. The plural is used here because whoever denies one messenger has denied all the messengers. It has been said: they disobeyed Hūd and those who came before him of messengers, or they were such that if Allah had sent to them many messengers, they would have denied them. ﴿And they followed the command of every obstinate tyrant﴾: *al-jabbār* is the arrogant one, and *al-ʿanīd* is the transgressor who does not accept the truth nor submit to it.

Abū ʿUbayda said: *al-ʿanīd* is *al-ʿanūd*, *al-ʿānid*, and *al-muʿānid*, the one who opposes by contradicting it from himself. From this it is said of a vein that bursts with blood: *ʿānid*.

The rajaz poet said:

*Indeed I am old, I cannot bear the stubborn ones.*

﴿And they were followed in this world by a curse﴾: that is, they were attached to it. It is being distanced from mercy and being expelled from good. The meaning is that it was constant for them, not leaving them as long as they were in this world, and on the Day of Resurrection they were followed by it, so they were cursed there just as they were cursed in this world. ﴿Unquestionably, ʿĀd disbelieved in their Lord﴾: that is, they disbelieved in their Lord.

al-Farrāʾ said: they disbelieved the blessing of their Lord. It is said: *kafartuhu* and *kafartu bihi*, like *shakartuhu* and *shakartu lahu*. ﴿Unquestionably, away with ʿĀd, the people of Hūd﴾: that is, may they never cease to be distanced from the mercy of Allah. *Bu'd* (distance) is destruction, and *bu'd* is remoteness from good. It is said: *baʿuda yabʿudu buʿdan* when he delayed and became distant, and *baʿuda yabʿudu buʿdan* when he perished. From this is the saying of the poet:

*Let not my people be far away, those who are the poison of enemies and the calamity of the slaughtered camels.*

And al-Nābigha said:

*So do not be far away, for death is a watering place, and every person's state will one day vanish.*

From this is the saying of the poet:

*What the words of their women benefited me, and I was killed in defense of their men, let them not be far.*

It has already been mentioned that the Arabs use it in invoking destruction.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Qatādah regarding ﴿except upon the One who originated me﴾: that is, created me.

Ibn ʿAsākir narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk who said: Allah withheld the rain from ʿĀd for three years. Hūd said to them: ﴿Seek forgiveness of your Lord, then repent to Him; He will send the sky upon you in abundance﴾, but they refused except to persist in their rebellion.

Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Hārūn al-Taymī regarding His saying: ﴿He will send the sky upon you in abundance﴾, that he said: the rain.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Mujāhid regarding His saying: ﴿And He will add strength to your strength﴾, that he said: might to your might.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from ʿIkrimah regarding His saying: ﴿And He will add strength to your strength﴾, that he said: the offspring of offspring.

Ibn Jarīr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying: ﴿We only say that some of our gods have struck you with some evil﴾, that he said: it has afflicted you with madness.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd who said: No one fears a hostile thief, or a fierce beast, or a rebellious devil and then recites this verse, except that Allah turns it away from him.

Ibn Jarīr and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is upon a straight path﴾, that he said: the truth.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Abū Mālik regarding His saying: ﴿A harsh punishment﴾, that he said: severe.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Qatādah regarding His saying: ﴿Every obstinate tyrant﴾, that he said: the polytheist.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from al-Suddī who said: *al-ʿanīd* is the one who opposes.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from al-Suddī regarding His saying: ﴿And they were followed in this world by a curse﴾, that he said: No prophet was sent after ʿĀd except that they were cursed upon his tongue.

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Qatādah regarding the verse, that he said: two curses from Allah followed them: a curse in this world, and a curse in the Hereafter.

Ḥafṣ narrated from ʿĀṣim that he recited *wa-yastakhlif* with a jazm (apocopation), taking it as modifying the position of ﴿I have already conveyed to you﴾. ﴿And you will not harm Him at all﴾: that is, by your turning away, and you will not be able to cause much harm or little. ﴿Indeed, my Lord is over all things a guardian﴾: that is, a watchful overseer over it who protects it from everything. It has been said: *ʿalā* here has the meaning of *li-* (for), so the meaning is "a guardian for everything," and so He protects me from your reaching me with any evil.

﴿And when Our command came﴾: that is, Our punishment, which is the destruction of ʿĀd, ﴿We saved Hūd and those who believed with him﴾ from among his people, ﴿by a mercy from Us﴾: that is, by a great mercy from Us, because no one is saved except by the mercy of Allah. It has been said that it is faith. ﴿From a harsh punishment﴾: that is, severe. It has been said that it was the *samūm* (scorching wind) which used to enter their noses.

﴿And those were ʿĀd﴾ is a subject and predicate, and the demonstrative was feminine in consideration of the tribe.

al-Kisāʾī said: among the Arabs are those who do not give *ʿĀd* the diptote-declension (*ṣarf*), and make it the name of the tribe. ﴿They denied the signs of their Lord﴾: that is, they disbelieved in them, denied them, and rejected the miracles. ﴿And they disobeyed His messengers﴾: that is, Hūd alone, because there was no other messenger in his time. The plural is used here because whoever denies one messenger has denied all the messengers. It has been said: they disobeyed Hūd and those who came before him of messengers, or they were such that if Allah had sent to them many messengers, they would have denied them. ﴿And they followed the command of every obstinate tyrant﴾: *al-jabbār* is the arrogant one, and *al-ʿanīd* is the transgressor who does not accept the truth nor submit to it.

Abū ʿUbayda said: *al-ʿanīd* is *al-ʿanūd*, *al-ʿānid*, and *al-muʿānid*, the one who opposes by contradicting it from himself. From this it is said of a vein that bursts with blood: *ʿānid*.

*Indeed I am old, I cannot bear the stubborn ones.*

*Let not my people be far away, those who are the poison of enemies and the calamity of the slaughtered camels.*

And al-Nābigha said:

*So do not be far away, for death is a watering place, and every person's state will one day vanish.*

From this is the saying of the poet:

*What the words of their women benefited me, and I was killed in defense of their men, let them not be far.*

It has already been mentioned that the Arabs use it in invoking destruction.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Qatādah regarding ﴿except upon the One who originated me﴾: that is, created me.

Ibn ʿAsākir narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk who said: Allah withheld the rain from ʿĀd for three years. Hūd said to them: ﴿Seek forgiveness of your Lord, then repent to Him; He will send the sky upon you in abundance﴾, but they refused except to persist in their rebellion.

Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Hārūn al-Taymī regarding His saying: ﴿He will send the sky upon you in abundance﴾, that he said: the rain.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Mujāhid regarding His saying: ﴿And He will add strength to your strength﴾, that he said: might to your might.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from ʿIkrimah regarding His saying: ﴿And He will add strength to your strength﴾, that he said: the offspring of offspring.

Ibn Jarīr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying: ﴿We only say that some of our gods have struck you with some evil﴾, that he said: it has afflicted you with madness.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd who said: No one fears a hostile thief, or a fierce beast, or a rebellious devil and then recites this verse, except that Allah turns it away from him.

Ibn Jarīr and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is upon a straight path﴾, that he said: the truth.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Abū Mālik regarding His saying: ﴿A harsh punishment﴾, that he said: severe.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Qatādah regarding His saying: ﴿Every obstinate tyrant﴾, that he said: the polytheist.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from al-Suddī who said: *al-ʿanīd* is the one who opposes.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from al-Suddī regarding His saying: ﴿And they were followed in this world by a curse﴾, that he said: No prophet was sent after ʿĀd except that they were cursed upon his tongue.

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Qatādah regarding the verse, that he said: two curses from Allah followed them: a curse in this world, and a curse in the Hereafter.

His saying, ﴿And to ʿĀd, their brother Hūd﴾, is coordinated with "And We sent Nūḥ" (*maʿṭūf ʿalā*). That is: and We sent to ʿĀd their brother, meaning one of them. Hūd is an explanatory apposition (*ʿaṭf bayān*, appositive clarification). The people of ʿĀd were worshippers of idols, and something similar has already been discussed in al-Aʿrāf.

It has been said: they are the First ʿĀd and the Last ʿĀd. The First ʿĀd and the Last ʿĀd are Shaddād and Luqmān and their people, who are mentioned in His saying, ﴿Iram of the lofty pillars﴾ [al-Fajr: 7]. The origin of "ʿĀd" is the name of a man, and then it became the name of a tribe, like Tamīm and Bakr and similar names.

﴿You have no god other than Him﴾: it is read *ghayruhu* with a kasra on the basis of the wording, and with a damma on the basis of the position of *min ilāhin* (the place of the word after the preposition), and it is read with a fatḥa as an exception (*istithnāʾ*). ﴿You are nothing but fabricators﴾: that is, you are not, in taking a god other than Allah, anything but liars against Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Then he addressed them, saying: ﴿O my people, I do not ask you for any reward for it﴾: that is, I do not seek from you any reward for what I convey to you and advise you about, of guidance to the worship of Allah alone and that you have no god besides Him. So the pronoun refers to the content of this speech.

The meaning of this has already been mentioned in the story of Nūḥ: ﴿My reward is only from the One who originated me﴾, that is, my reward that I seek is only from the One who originated me, meaning created me; He is the One who will reward me for that. ﴿Will you not reason?﴾ that the reward of those who give sincere advice is only from the Lord of the worlds. It has been said: in what preceded, in the story of Nūḥ, he said *mālan* (wealth), but here he said *ajran* (reward), because of the mention of the treasuries after it in the story of Nūḥ, and the word "wealth" is more fitting there.

Then he guided them to seeking forgiveness and repentance.

The meaning is: seek His forgiveness for what has passed of your sins, then draw near to Him through repentance.

A fuller explanation of something similar has already been given in the story of Nūḥ. Then he encouraged them to believe with the promise of immediate good, saying: ﴿He will send the sky﴾, that is, the rain, ﴿upon you in abundance﴾, that is, abundant in its pouring. It is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (*ḥāl*). The sky poured, pours, and so it is abundant (*midrār*). The people of Hūd were people of gardens, crops, and prosperity, and their dwellings were the sands that lay between al-Shām and al-Yaman. ﴿And He will add strength to your strength﴾ is coordinated with "He will send": that is, added might to your might, or fertility to your fertility, or honor to your honor.

al-Zajjāj said: the meaning is "He will add to you strength in blessings."

﴿And do not turn away as criminals﴾: that is, do not turn away from what I call you to and persist in disbelief, insisting upon it. *Ijrām* (criminality) means sins, as has already been mentioned.

Then his people answered him with what indicates their extreme ignorance and great stupidity: ﴿They said, "O Hūd, you have not brought us any clear proof"﴾, that is, any evident argument that we could act upon and believe you on account of it, while not acknowledging the proofs and demonstrations of Allah that had come to them, out of obstinacy and distance from the truth. ﴿And we will not abandon our gods﴾ which we worship besides Allah.

The meaning of ﴿on your word﴾ is "departing from your word," so the adverbial phrase is in the accusative place as a circumstantial state. ﴿And we are not believers in you﴾: that is, we will not believe you regarding anything of what you have brought.

﴿We only say that some of our gods have struck you with some evil﴾: that is, we say only that some of our gods, which you disparage and which you deem foolish in our worship, have afflicted you with evil, namely madness, so that what you say to us and repeat to us of warning against them has arisen from your madness. It is said: *ʿarāhu al-amr* and *iʿtarāhu* means when a matter befalls him.

So he answered them with what indicates his indifference to them, his confidence in his Lord, and his reliance upon Him, and that they have no power over anything that the disbelievers want to do to him; rather, Allah, glorified is He, is the One who harms and benefits. So ﴿He said, "I call Allah to witness, and you bear witness"﴾ that ﴿I am free from what you associate﴾ with Him.

﴿Besides Him﴾: that is, from your associating others with Allah besides Allah, without Allah having sent down any authority for it. ﴿So scheme against me, all of you﴾: you and your gods, if they are as you claim, able to harm me and that they have afflicted me with evil. ﴿Then do not give me respite﴾: that is, do not delay me, but hasten against me and do what you will. In this there is a display of indifference to them and to their idols, which they worship, that would strike their ears, and it makes clear their helplessness and their inability over anything.

﴿Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord﴾: so He will protect me from your scheming, and even if you reach every extent in seeking ways to harm me, whoever relies upon Allah, He suffices him.

Then, when he had shown them his reliance upon Allah and his confidence in His protection and guardianship, he described Him with what necessitates reliance upon Him and entrusting oneself to Him: that His lordship encompasses Him and them, and that He is the owner of all things, and that the forelock of every creature among the creatures of the earth is in His hand, in His grip and under His subjugation. This is an image of the utmost subjugation and the ultimate humbling. When they took a captive and wanted to release him and bestow favor upon him, they would cut his forelock, making that a sign of his subjugation.

al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning of *ākhidhun bi-nāṣiyatihā* (one who takes hold of its forelock) is its owner and the one who has power over it. al-Qutaybī said: its subduer, because whoever you take by the forelock, you have subdued him. The *nāṣiyah* is the hair at the front of the head.

Then he gave the reason for what preceded with his saying: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is upon a straight path﴾: that is, He is upon truth and justice, so He hardly lets you dominate me.

﴿But if you turn away﴾: that is, you are persisting in turning away, so one of the two *tāʾs* was dropped. Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 11, verse 61–68:

His saying: ﴿And to Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih﴾ is coordinated with what preceded, and the implied meaning is: "And We sent to Thamud their brother Salih." The discussion regarding it, and regarding His saying ﴿O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him﴾, is as it was mentioned in the story of Hud.

Al-Hasan and Yahya ibn Wathhab read "wa-ila Thamudin" with tanwin (nunation) in all instances.

The rest of the readers differed regarding it: they gave it diptote treatment (ṣarf) in one place and did not in another. The ṣarf (declension with tanwin) is based on interpreting it as referring to a living group (ḥayy), and the non-ṣarf (diptote, without tanwin) is based on interpreting it as referring to a tribe (qabīla). Likewise for everything that admits of both interpretations. Sibawayh recited, regarding the feminine treatment based on interpreting it as a tribe:

"The Walid overcame the generous ones as a group, and he sufficed Quraysh in the difficult matters and was their master."

His saying: ﴿He produced you from the earth﴾ means He originated your creation from the earth, because all the children of Adam are from the loins of Adam, and he was created from the earth. ﴿And settled you therein﴾ means He made you its inhabitants and residents, from the saying of people: "So-and-so settled (a'mara) so-and-so in his house, so it is for him as a lifelong grant ('umrā)." Thus istaf'ala here carries the meaning of af'ala, like istajaba meaning ajaba.

Al-Dahhak said: its meaning is that He lengthened your lifespans, and their lifespans ranged from three hundred to a thousand years. It was also said that its meaning is: He commanded you to cultivate it, through building dwellings and planting trees. ﴿So seek His forgiveness﴾ means ask Him to forgive you for worshipping idols. ﴿Then turn in repentance to Him﴾ means return to worshipping Him. ﴿Indeed, my Lord is near and responsive﴾ means near in responding to whoever calls upon Him. The discussion of this has preceded in al-Baqarah at His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed I am near; I respond to the invocation of the supplicant﴾ [al-Baqarah: 186].

﴿They said, "O Salih, you were among us a man of hope before this﴾ means: we used to hope that you would be among us a noble leader whose opinion we would benefit from and whose leadership would bring us happiness, before this that you have shown—your claim to prophethood and your call to monotheism. It was also said: Salih used to disparage their gods, and they hoped he would return to their religion; when he called them to Allah they said, "Our hope in you has been cut off." The interrogation in His saying ﴿Do you forbid us that we worship what our fathers worshipped?﴾ is for denial; they denied this prohibition from him. "That we worship" is in a position of accusative by the deletion of the preposition, i.e., "from [or: in] worshipping." The meaning of "what our fathers worshipped" is "what our fathers used to worship," so it is a narration of a past state in order to bring the image to mind. ﴿And indeed we are in disquieting doubt concerning that to which you invite us﴾: from arabtuhu, "I make him doubtful," when I do to him an act that causes him ril-ba (uneasiness), which is restlessness of the soul and absence of tranquility; or from arāba al-rajul, when a man becomes one who has ribah. The meaning is: indeed we are in doubt about what you call us to—worshipping Allah alone—and abandoning the worship of idols causes doubt.

﴿He said, "O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord﴾ means a manifest proof and a sound demonstration, ﴿and He has given me from Himself mercy﴾ means from His side, mercy, that is, prophethood. Although these matters are certain in occurrence, they were introduced with the word of doubt in consideration of the state of the addressees, because they are in doubt about that, as they described themselves. ﴿Then who would support me against Allah?﴾ is an interrogation whose meaning is negation: that is, there is no supporter for me to prevent me from the punishment of Allah ﴿if I disobey Him﴾ in conveying the message, and I become lax and slacken in what is obligatory upon me of conveyance. ﴿So you would not increase me﴾ by your discouraging me ﴿except in loss﴾ by making me a loser through the nullification of my deed and exposing me to the punishment of Allah.

Al-Farra' said: that is, misguidance and distance from good. It was also said the meaning is: you would not increase me, by your insistence upon the religion of your fathers, except without insight into your own loss.

His saying: ﴿And O my people, this is the she-camel of Allah, a sign for you﴾ — the explanation of this verse has already passed in al-A'raf. The meaning of ﴿a sign for you﴾ is a clear miracle, and it is in accusative position as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl). "For you" is in a position of accusative as a circumstantial clause from "sign," which precedes it; had it come after, it would have been a qualifier of it. It was also said: "the she-camel of Allah" is an apposition (badal) of "this," and the predicate is "for you," but the first is preferable. He said "the she-camel of Allah" because He brought it out for them from a mountain according to their demand; and it was also said: from a solid rock. ﴿So leave her to eat in the earth of Allah﴾ means: let her be, to eat in the earth of Allah from what is in it of pastures that animals eat.

Abu Ishaq al-Zajjaj said: it is permissible to read "ta'kul" in the nominative as a circumstantial clause and as a resumed sentence, though he perhaps meant this in the original linguistic sense permitted by Arabic and not within the verse itself; the relied-upon readings are those transmitted in a sound manner. ﴿And do not touch her with harm﴾.

Al-Farra' said: with slaughter (ʿaqr). The apparent meaning is that the prohibition concerns what is more general than that. ﴿Lest a near punishment seize you﴾: this is the response to the prohibition, meaning: near to her slaughter, and that was three days.

﴿So they slaughtered her﴾, meaning they did not comply with the command from Salih nor the prohibition, but opposed all of that, so the slaughter of her occurred from them. Then Salih said to them: ﴿Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days﴾, meaning: enjoy living in your dwellings for three days, for the punishment will descend upon you after them. It was said: they slaughtered her on Wednesday, then they remained through Thursday, Friday, and Saturday, and the punishment came to them on Sunday. The reference in His saying "that" is to what the command to enjoy oneself for three days indicates. ﴿A promise not to be denied﴾: that is, a promise not denied in it; the preposition is deleted by extension, or it is by way of metaphor, as if the promise, when it is fulfilled, is true and not false. It is also permissible that it be a verbal noun: that is, a promise that is not a lie.

﴿So when Our command came﴾, that is, Our punishment, or Our command to the occurrence of the punishment, ﴿We saved Salih and those who believed with him by mercy from Us﴾. The explanation of this has already passed in the story of Hud. ﴿And from the disgrace of that day﴾: that is, and We saved them from the disgrace of that day, which is their destruction by the Blast; and khizy is humiliation and abasement. It was also said: from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, but the first is preferable.

Nafi' and al-Kisa'i read "yawma" with a fatha, on the basis that it has taken on indeclinability from the noun it is annexed to. The rest read it with a kasra.

﴿Indeed, your Lord is the Powerful, the Mighty﴾: the Capable, the Dominant, whom nothing can render powerless.

﴿And the cry seized those who had wronged﴾: that is, on the fourth day from the slaughter of the she-camel, they were struck with a cry and died. The verb is masculine because "al-sayha" and "al-siyah" are one, and the feminine is not real. It was said it was the cry of Jibril; it was also said a cry from the sky, so their hearts were torn apart and they died. It has passed in al-A'raf: ﴿so the earthquake seized them﴾ [al-A'raf: 78]. It was said: perhaps it occurred right after the cry. ﴿So they became in their homes prostrate﴾: that is, fallen upon their faces, dead, clinging to the dust like birds when they crouch.

﴿As if they had never flourished therein﴾: that is, as if they had never resided in their lands or dwellings. Likewise for everything that admits of both interpretations. Sibawayh recited, regarding the feminine treatment based on interpreting it as a tribe:

﴿They said, "O Salih, you were among us a man of hope before this﴾ means: we used to hope that you would be among us a noble leader whose opinion we would benefit from and whose leadership would bring us happiness, before this that you have shown—your claim to prophethood and your call to monotheism. It was also said: Salih used to disparage their gods, and they hoped he would return to their religion; when he called them to Allah they said, "Our hope in you has been cut off." The interrogation in His saying ﴿Do you forbid us that we worship what our fathers worshipped?﴾ is for denial; they denied this prohibition from him. "That we worship" is in a position of accusative by the deletion of the preposition, i.e., "from [or: in] worshipping." His saying: ﴿And to Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih﴾ is coordinated with what preceded, and the implied meaning is: "And We sent to Thamud their brother Salih." The discussion regarding it, and regarding His saying ﴿O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him﴾, is as it was mentioned in the story of Hud.

Al-Hasan and Yahya ibn Wathhab read "wa-ila Thamudin" with tanwin (nunation) in all instances.

The rest of the readers differed regarding it: they gave it diptote treatment (ṣarf) in one place and did not in another. The ṣarf (declension with tanwin) is based on interpreting it as referring to a living group (ḥayy), and the non-ṣarf (diptote, without tanwin) is based on interpreting it as referring to a tribe (qabīla). Likewise for everything that admits of both interpretations. Sibawayh recited, regarding the feminine treatment based on interpreting it as a tribe:

"The Walid overcame the generous ones as a group, and he sufficed Quraysh in the difficult matters and was their master."

His saying: ﴿He produced you from the earth﴾ means He originated your creation from the earth, because all the children of Adam are from the loins of Adam, and he was created from the earth. ﴿And settled you therein﴾ means He made you its inhabitants and residents, from the saying of people: "So-and-so settled (a'mara) so-and-so in his house, so it is for him as a lifelong grant ('umrā)." Thus istaf'ala here carries the meaning of af'ala, like istajaba meaning ajaba.

Al-Dahhak said: its meaning is that He lengthened your lifespans, and their lifespans ranged from three hundred to a thousand years. It was also said that its meaning is: He commanded you to cultivate it, through building dwellings and planting trees. ﴿So seek His forgiveness﴾ means ask Him to forgive you for worshipping idols. ﴿Then turn in repentance to Him﴾ means return to worshipping Him. ﴿Indeed, my Lord is near and responsive﴾ means near in responding to whoever calls upon Him. The discussion of this has preceded in al-Baqarah at His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed I am near; I respond to the invocation of the supplicant﴾ [al-Baqarah: 186].

﴿They said, "O Salih, you were among us a man of hope before this﴾ means: we used to hope that you would be among us a noble leader whose opinion we would benefit from and whose leadership would bring us happiness, before this that you have shown—your claim to prophethood and your call to monotheism. It was also said: Salih used to disparage their gods, and they hoped he would return to their religion; when he called them to Allah they said, "Our hope in you has been cut off." The interrogation in His saying ﴿Do you forbid us that we worship what our fathers worshipped?﴾ is for denial; they denied this prohibition from him. "That we worship" is in a position of accusative by the deletion of the preposition, i.e., "from [or: in] worshipping." The meaning of "what our fathers worshipped" is "what our fathers used to worship," so it is a narration of a past state in order to bring the image to mind. ﴿And indeed we are in disquieting doubt concerning that to which you invite us﴾: from arabtuhu, "I make him doubtful," when I do to him an act that causes him ril-ba (uneasiness), which is restlessness of the soul and absence of tranquility; or from arāba al-rajul, when a man becomes one who has ribah. Al-Hasan and Yahya ibn Wathhab read "wa-ila Thamudin" with tanwin (nunation) in all instances.

This is the commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 11, verses 69–76 (part 1 of 2):

.
This is the story of Lut (Lot), peace be upon him, and his people. He was the paternal cousin of Ibrahim (Abraham), peace be upon him. The towns of Lut were in the regions of al-Sham (Greater Syria), and Ibrahim was in the land of Palestine.

When Allah sent the angels with the punishment for the people of Lut, they passed by Ibrahim and stopped at his place. Whoever stopped at his place, he would treat generously as a guest. Their passing by him was to give him this good news mentioned here. He thought them to be guests, and they were Jibril (Gabriel), Mika'il (Michael), and Israfil (Raphael).

It has been said they were nine, and it has been said they were eleven. The good news they gave him was the news of a son, and it has been said it was the news of the destruction of the people of Lut. The first view is the better one. ﴿They said, "Peace."﴾ Salaman (peace) is in the accusative because it is governed by a verb that is understood: that is, "We greet you with peace." ﴿He said, "Peace."﴾ Its nominative case is because it is the predicate of an omitted subject: that is, "Your affair is peace." Or it is nominative because it is the subject, and the predicate is omitted, and the estimated meaning is: "Upon you is peace."

﴿So he did not delay⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿ ﻿﻿﻿—﻿that is, Ibrahim—﻿in bringing a roasted calf.﴾ Most of the grammarians say that "an" (that) here means "hatta" (until): that is, "So he did not delay until he brought." It has been said that it is in the accusative position after the removal of the preposition (ḥarf al-jarr), and the estimated meaning is: "So he did not delay in coming with a calf," meaning Ibrahim was not slow in bringing a calf. "Ma" is a negation. This is what Sibawayh said.

Al-Farra' said: "So his delay was not (his coming)," meaning his coming was not slow. It has also been said that "ma" is a relative pronoun and is the subject, and the predicate is "an ja'a bi-'ijlin ḥanidh" (that he came with a roasted calf). The estimated meaning is: "What Ibrahim delayed was his coming with a roasted calf."

Ḥanidh means roasted in general. It has been said it means roasted by the heat of stones without the fire touching it. It is said: "Hanadha ash-shāta yaḥnidhuhā" meaning he placed the sheep over heated stones to cook it, so it is ḥanidh. It has been said that the meaning of ḥanidh is fat. It has been said ḥanidh is samīṭ (skinned and roasted). It has also been said it is nadīj (well-cooked). It is a form (faʿīl) in the sense of a passive participle (maf'ūl). He brought them a calf because cattle was most of his wealth.

﴿When he saw their hands not reaching toward it⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿—﻿that is, they did not reach out to the calf as a person who wants to eat would reach out his hand—﻿he was suspicious of them.⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿ (p-665) It is said: "Nakirtahu, wa-ankartahu, wa-istankartahu," meaning when you find someone in a state other than what you are accustomed to. From this is the saying of the poet:

She disowned me, and what she disowned of the events
was nothing but gray hair and baldness.

So he combined the two dialects. Among the examples where the two dialects are combined is the saying of the poet:

When a land disowns me, or I disown it,
I went out with the falcon, and blackness was upon me.

It has also been said: "Ankartu" is used for what you see with your eye, and "nakirtu" for what you see with your heart. It has been said: He was suspicious of them because their custom was that when a guest came to them and did not eat their food, they thought he had come with evil intent.

﴿And he felt fear of them⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿—﻿that is, he sensed within himself a fear, meaning dread and alarm. It has been said the meaning of awjasa is that he concealed fear within himself. The first meaning is closer to the linguistic meaning. From this is the saying of the poet:

The messenger came with a letter urging him,
and the heart felt fear from its letter, alarmed.

It seems he thought they had come to him for a matter he disapproved of, or for the punishment of his people. ﴿They said, "Do not fear."⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿ They said this to him even though he had not spoken anything indicating fear; rather, he felt it within himself. Perhaps they inferred his fear from signs such as the effect of it appearing on his face. Or they said it to him after he said, following what he felt within himself of dread, a statement indicating fear, as in His saying in Surat al-Hijr: ﴿He said, "Indeed, we are fearful of you."﴾ [Al-Hijr: 52]. This was not mentioned here, being sufficient with what is there.

Then they gave the reason for prohibiting his fear by saying: ﴿Indeed, we have been sent to the people of Lut.﴾ That is, we have been sent to them specifically. It is possible that Ibrahim, peace be upon him, said a statement to which this would be the answer: ﴿He said, "What is your business, O messengers?" They said, "Indeed, we have been sent to a criminal people."﴾ [Al-Hijr: 57–58].

The clause ﴿and his wife was standing and she laughed⁠

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 11, verse 69–76 (part 2 of 2):

Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah, who said: When Ibrahim sensed fear within himself, they (the angels) told him then what they had come for, and his wife laughed in wonder at the heedlessness of the people of Lut and at the punishment that had come upon them.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿فَضَحِكَتْ﴾ ("then she laughed"), who said: She menstruated, and she was ninety-eight years old.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Mujahid regarding His words ﴿فَضَحِكَتْ﴾, who said: She menstruated, and she was about ninety years old, while Ibrahim was one hundred years old.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ikrimah, who said: She menstruated.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Umar the same as this.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His words ﴿ومِن وراءِ إسْحاقَ يَعْقُوبَ﴾ ("and after Ishaq, Ya'qub"), who said: He is the son's son.

Ibn al-Anbari, in his book al-Waqf wa al-Ibtida' (On Pausing and Starting), narrated from Hassan ibn Abjar, who said: I was with Ibn Abbas when a man from Hudhayl came. Ibn Abbas said to him: "What did so-and-so do?" He said: "He died and left four sons and three from among the descendants (al-waraʾ)." Ibn Abbas said: ﴿فَبَشَّرْناها بِإسْحاقَ ومِن وراءِ إسْحاقَ يَعْقُوبَ﴾ and said: "The son's son."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, Abu al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman narrated through several chains from Ibn Abbas that he used to forbid adding to the reply to the greeting beyond their saying: "ʿAlaykum al-salam wa rahmat Allah wa barakatuh," and he would recite this verse: ﴿رَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وبَرَكاتُهُ عَلَيْكم أهْلَ البَيْتِ﴾ ("The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, O people of the household").

Al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Umar something similar.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid regarding His words ﴿فَلَمّا ذَهَبَ عَنْ إبْراهِيمَ الرَّوْعُ﴾ ("When the fear had left Ibrahim"), who said: "Al-faraq" (the fright/alarm). ﴿يُجادِلُنا في قَوْمِ لُوطٍ﴾ ("he argued with us concerning the people of Lut"), who said: "He disputed with us."

Abd al-Razzaq and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah regarding the explanation of al-mujadalah (the arguing), who said: He said to them on that day: "What do you think if there are fifty Muslims among them?" They said: "If there are fifty among them, we will not punish them." He said: "Forty?" They said: "And forty." He said: "Thirty?" They said: "And thirty," until they reached ten. They said: "If there are ten among them, we will not punish them." He said: "What of a people among whom there are not ten, is there any good in them?" Qatadah said: In the town of Lut there were four thousand thousand people, or as much of that as Allah willed.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the angels came to Ibrahim, they said to Ibrahim: "If there are five among them who pray, the punishment will be lifted from them."

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Amr ibn Maymun, who said: "Al-awwah" is "the compassionate."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Al-munib" is "the one who turns back (in repentance) to the obedience of Allah."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatadah, who said: "Al-munib" is "the sincere."
